articles.title: 49ers Owner Jed York Pleads No Contest to Two Misdemeanor Charges in Ohio
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio and pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio and pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.

Court records show that York initially was charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct. York was charged with possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to an undercover online prostitution advertisement, according to prosecutors.

York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio, near where he was born and raised in Youngstown. He was released after posting a $5,000 bond. He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offenses to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest Monday morning. He also was fined $1,150.

York Responded to Ad on Prostitution Site Before Arrest

Records also show that York had his cellphone returned to him and that $160 that was seized was to be given to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force as part of the plea agreement. York also completed an online course.

Columbiana County Prosecutor Vito Abruzzino said most of these prostitution cases typically end in plea agreements.

"Each case is looked at individually and for specific facts of the conduct, what evidence the police provide, and input from the arresting officer," he said in an email. "You also have to factor in criminal history of the defendant, and whether or not they have committed these types of offenses in the past, and importantly, what the judges will allow."

The NFL issued a statement saying the league was aware of the arrest and would review it under the personal conduct policy. Owners are subject to possible fines or suspensions for violating the personal conduct policy. New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft was investigated but not punished by the league after he was arrested in Florida in 2019 for allegedly paying for sex with a woman at a massage parlor. The charge was later dropped after a court ruled that police violated the rights of Kraft and the other customers when they secretly installed video cameras inside massage rooms at the spa.

The team said it would not have any comment on the situation.

"As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time," the team said in a statement.

York took over day-to-day control of the 49ers from his parents in 2008. He became the team's principal owner in 2024. After some initial struggles under York's leadership, the team has been a consistent contender since hiring coach Kyle Shanahan and general manager John Lynch in 2017.

The Niners have made the Super Bowl three times under York's leadership, losing in the 2012 season under coach Jim Harbaugh and the 2019 and '23 seasons under Shanahan and Lynch.

York also oversaw the building of Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California. The team moved from San Francisco to the new stadium in 2014. The stadium has hosted two Super Bowls, a World Cup and a College Football Playoff title game.

articles.title: 'Hot Dog Fridge' Eyed by New Cowboys OC Klayton Adams and Explains Full Vision for Break Room
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys offensive coordinator Klayton Adams has lobbied for a very special addition to the coaching staff's break room.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys offensive coordinator Klayton Adams has lobbied for a very special addition to the coaching staff's break room.

Adams told reporters earlier this month he wants to get a "hot dog fridge" for himself and his fellow coaches.

"How can you really have a break room or a snack room if you don't have a hot dog fridge?" he said And if you're gonna have a hot dog fridge, you have to have high quality hot dogs in it. And if you're gonna have high quality hot dogs, we have to have brioche buns and maybe some pretzel buns."

🎥 Pickens' Trash Talk from Joint Practice

He suggested the solution could be "an industrial-sized 7-Eleven hot dog roller."

The comments came after the Cowboys shared a video of Adams being mic'd up at practice. At one point, he tells another Cowboys staffer they'd have to add $100 to the hot dog fridge fund.

This is something Adams has carefully considered, down to the science required to getting the perfect dog.

"One of the things I learned from going to Disneyland with my kids, because I was trying to steam the bun, I was trying to toast the bun, and the guy at Disneyland goes, 'No, man, put it in the bun and then wrap it in foil and let the hot dog steam the bun,'" he said. "It's been revolutionary."

The Cowboys had a top-10 offense in yards and points in Adams' first year as the coordinator. If that doesn't earn somebody a hot dog fridge, then what does?

articles.title: New Steelers Rumors on Joey Porter Jr.'s Contract amid NFL Trade Buzz and Mike McCarthy's Comments
articles.summary: As the start of the 2026 NFL season draws nearer, the Pittsburgh Steelers are still struggling to keep one of their key defensive players happy.
articles.body:
As the start of the 2026 NFL season draws nearer, the Pittsburgh Steelers are still struggling to keep one of their key defensive players happy.

Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy told reporters on Monday that the team is at an "impasse" in contract negotiations with cornerback Joey Porter Jr., and ESPN's Brooke Pryor reported that sources said that "there hasn't been any meaningful progress in extension talks." A source also told Pryor that the Steelers "haven't made or received any trade calls on Porter."

Porter is entering the final year of his rookie contract after being selected by the Steelers in the second round of the 2023 NFL draft. He reportedly aggravated a back injury during a mobility workout on the first day of training camp and was placed on the physically unable to perform list.

When asked about a potential timeline for Porter's return to the field ahead of Pittsburgh's Week 1 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons, McCarthy candidly admitted that his contract situation makes it tough to predict when things will be resolved.

"I learned this in my early years as a head coach, you have to separate the business and football," McCarthy said. "Sometimes it's easier in others. This is a challenge for both Joey and us because we're first-year staff. We've seen them play, compete against Joey. I would love the opportunity to coach Joey Porter. I know our defensive guys would love the opportunity. So we're at an impasse right here, and you got to respect that. Every one of us has a contract. The organization, they have beliefs and so forth. But yeah, that's just kind of where we are."

Despite Porter's injury and contract dispute, he's remained professional. Pryor noted that he's been present at training camp practices, usually watching from the sidelines. Defensive coordinator Patrick Graham also said the 26-year-old has been "engaged" in the classroom during his stint on the PUP list.

Still, it's safe to say that the Steelers would prefer to keep Porter happy and healthy as they try to chase a playoff spot during the upcoming season.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders' Reaction to Deshaun Watson Being Named Browns' QB1 Revealed by Todd Monken
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken addressed his decision Monday to name Deshaun Watson the starting quarterback over Shedeur Sanders.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken addressed his decision Monday to name Deshaun Watson the starting quarterback over Shedeur Sanders.

Monken said Sanders had an "awesome" reaction to learning he'll be the backup in Week 1.

"You talk about somebody that really understands the long game," the coach told reporters. "That really I think has come to understand the long game. What are we really in this for? What am I in it for? ... Where do we want to be in the long term? He understands that as well as a quarterback."

Monken praised Sanders' work to continue developing ahead of his second season. However, he believes Watson is a better option under center right now, especially since the team starts on the road against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

To some extent, Monken might be taking a longer view of the situation himself.

Any goodwill toward Watson is pretty much gone at this point. The majority of fans will have wanted Sanders to get the keys to the offense.

Now imagine Cleveland getting off to a poor start and Watson delivering more of the same from his first three years with the team — two things that can plausibly happen. The support behind Sanders will be even larger, and he'll get judged even less on the Browns' overall fortunes.

This might be applying too much game theory to Monken's decision. Coaches rarely go into a season trying to lose games, even when their team is rebuilding.

And it doesn't represent a strong endorsement of Sanders that he's not head and shoulders better than a veteran who has been in a years-long decline. Watson's last productive year under center was in 2020.

When Cleveland is widely projected to be one of the NFL's worst teams, why not pin your hopes to the player with far more long-term upside?

Hiring a new coach presents an opportunity for a franchise to wipe the slate clean, and it's way too early to make any concrete judgments about Monken. He probably hasn't made a great first impression on the fans, who are asking whether they'll witness more of the same futility and dysfunction from previous years.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders' time is running out
articles.summary: Sanders had a chance to win the Browns' starting job. He didn't. Now, with Cleveland turning back to Deshaun Watson, the clock is ticking on Sanders' opportu...
articles.body:
Here's a little thought experiment that's going to tie into the Cleveland Browns' decision to start Deshaun Watson over Shedeur Sanders , I promise:

When's the last time you sat down at a specific, prescribed time to watch a TV show? At, say, 8 p.m. on a Thursday or 9 p.m. on a Saturday? Probably been years, even decades, right? We're in an on-demand world now, where viewers hold the power. There's no such thing as prime time — you can see where this is going, I bet — any more.

Sanders arrived in the NFL on a tsunami of hype, whipped up and fueled by his famous father. Now, it's not unusual for dads to overestimate the skills of their sons — that's the foundation of the entire youth sports industrial complex, after all — but when your father is Deion "Prime Time" Sanders, well, dad's bellowing from the sideline carries a whole lot further.

We don't need to re-litigate everything from Shedeur's career that led him from his father's house to the Cleveland sideline — the decent-but-not-spectacular college career, the fifth-round NFL Draft selection that was either a stunning plunge or a proper assessment, the rookie season that pinballed between glory and agony. What's indisputable is this:

Sanders had every chance to claim the Browns' starting QB job for himself. Hell, the Browns surely wanted Sanders to seize the job, if only so that they could start to distance themselves from a frontrunner for the worst trade and worst contract in NFL history. And he didn't get it done.

The opportunity was there. In 2025, Sanders started the final seven games of the Browns' lost season — in Cleveland, is there any other kind? — and led the team to a 3-4 record. Over the course of the offseason, the Browns focused their free-agency efforts on positions other than quarterback, suggesting that new head coach Todd Monken was happy to stand pat with his current hand of QBs — Sanders, Watson, Dillon Gabriel and rookie Taylen Green . (Whether this was a defensible strategy is a different question.)

Over the weekend, Sanders, who started against Buffalo on Saturday, was decent but not necessarily spectacular, going 9-of-11 for 74 yards with a touchdown and a behind-the-receiver interception. Watson, meanwhile, went three-and-out on his first two drives, leading to boos from the Browns' grandstands. Watson would later call those boos "disrespectful," not exactly what you want to hear from your starting QB — or your fans — with just a few weeks left until Week 1.

Play Yahoo's new College Fantasy Football game: Create or join a league now!

Monken appears to be siding with Watson for his veteran presence and, well, not much else. Watson hasn't played since October 2024. Sidelined by both suspension and injury, he's seen action in just 19 of a possible 85 Browns games since joining Cleveland after the 2020 season. With a contract too massive to escape or pawn off on anyone else, the Browns had little choice but to see what, if anything, they could wring out of Watson.

So where does that leave Sanders? On a rapidly shrinking island.

Already legendary for churning through quarterbacks over the course of its history, Cleveland started an incredible five different QBs in 2023, four in 2024 and three, including Sanders, last season. If Shedeur wasn't able to fight his way out of that dogpile, what does that say about his prospects going forward?

Sanders' supporters love to claim he hasn't received a fair shake — it's the same complaint that Tim Tebow 's disciples lodged, year after subpar year — and the fact that Watson got the majority of first-team reps in preseason will only fuel that ongoing conspiracy. But if Watson struggles — and Monken has made it clear he expects immediate results — Sanders should get yet another opportunity to prove himself. The question now ahead of Sanders: How many more of those opportunities will he squander?

Prime Time is already history. And now Shedeur Sanders is quickly running out of time to carve his own space, too.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson Apologizes for Slamming Browns Fans Booing Him After Todd Monken Meeting
articles.summary: After Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson fired back at fans for booing him during the team's second preseason game on Saturday, he reversed course after a meeting with head coach Todd Monken.
articles.body:
After Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson fired back at fans for booing him during the team's second preseason game on Saturday, he reversed course after a meeting with head coach Todd Monken.

Watson opened his media availability on Monday with an apology for his comments, admitting that emotions got the better of him:

Shedeur's Reaction to Browns' QB Decision

Monken said he spoke to Watson about his comments calling out fans for their reaction to him on the field.

"The conversation was, 'The way we make this go away is play good football. We've got to own that,'" Monken told reporters on Monday. "I asked him, 'Do you feel like you got that off your chest?' Now what do we do? Move forward."

Watson played four second-half drives in Saturday's 31-7 preseason loss against the Buffalo Bills, going 5-of-7 for 36 yards and an interception. While his subpar play certainly didn't sit well with the Cleveland crowd, the 30-year-old asserted that the boos weren't based on what he did on the field.

"I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance," Watson said after the game . "It's a little bit [more] personal than that. So I think it's a disrespectful thing. So yeah, I mean, I'm going to keep whatever I feel with me and my family internally on how I feel about that. And yeah, just move on."

Despite his lackluster showing on Saturday, Watson was named Cleveland's starting quarterback for the 2026 season on Monday over second-year signal-caller Shedeur Sanders. It remains to be seen if his apology will be enough to win back some fans.

Watson will be hoping to avoid any further battles with Browns fans when the team opens the 2026 season on Sept. 13 against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson's 'Poison Pill' in Contract Reported After Winning Browns' QB1 over Shedeur Sanders
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns made the astonishing decision to name Deshaun Watson their starting quarterback on Monday, though releasing him was never really an option.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns made the astonishing decision to name Deshaun Watson their starting quarterback on Monday, though releasing him was never really an option.

As Spotrac noted, doing so would have incurred an $86.2 million dead cap hit for the 2027 season. However, that can be spread between two seasons if he's cut before March 13 in 2027 and designated a post-June 1 release, which would also avoid a $200 million guaranteed salary poison pill:

Shedeur's Reaction to Browns' QB Decision

The decision to not only trade for Watson, but also give him a fully-guaranteed contract, remains one of the worst decisions in modern sports history.

Here's what the Browns have gotten for the three first-round picks, one third-rounder, two fourths and the $230 million in fully guaranteed salary over five seasons it took to acquire Watson: 19 total starts, 3,365 yards, 19 touchdowns, 12 interceptions, a 61.2 completion percentage and a 9-10 record.

And after finishing 5-of-12 passes for 35 yards and an interception during Saturday's preseason game, Watson was booed by Cleveland's home crowd and didn't further endear himself to the fan base after the contest.

"I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance," he told reporters regarding the boos. "It's a little bit [more] personal than that. So I think it's a disrespectful thing. So yeah, I mean, I'm going to keep whatever I feel with me and my family internally on how I feel about that. And yeah, just move on. ... Last time I played on this field, I tore my Achilles. And that same fanbase, they cheered when I got hurt. So what does that have to do with anything about performance? When a person gets hurt, especially for your own city, and they cheer?"

It's more complicated than that, of course. Alongside his disappointing performance, Watson's contract has been prohibitive from a team-building standpoint and he also had past scandals that soured him in the eyes of many fans.

He apologized for his remarks on Monday:

It's a virtual guarantee that Watson will not be on the Browns' roster in 2027. He'll leave behind plenty of dead cap space and a strained relationship with Cleveland fans, however.

articles.summary: The principal owner of the NFL’s San Francisco 49ers was arrested on Sunday and accused of “engaging in prostitution” in Ohio, according to court documents obtained by CNN.

Jed York, who’s been with the team for nearly 20 years, became the chief executive officer in 2010. The documents state York paid $1,150 in fines associated with the charges and sentenced to a night in jail. CNN has reached out to the 49ers and York’s legal team for comment. articles.title: Patriots, Texans Make Surprise Kayshon Boutte Trade After Higgins' Injury, New NFL Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: The New England Patriots are reportedly trading wideout Kayshon Boutte to the Houston Texans for safety Jaylen Reed and a draft pick, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots are reportedly trading wideout Kayshon Boutte to the Houston Texans for safety Jaylen Reed and a draft pick, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero .

Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported the Patriots will get a seventh-round pick in the deal:

The deal comes in the wake of Houston receiver Jayden Higgins suffering a season-ending ACL tear.

Boutte, 24, caught 78 passes for 1,159 yards and nine touchdowns in his three seasons for the Patriots after being a sixth-round pick in the 2023 NFL draft.

But with the Patriots adding A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs in the offseason, DeMario Douglas set to handle slot duties , Kyle Williams impressing during the preseason and both Mack Hollins and Efton Chism III available as depth, Boutte was clearly expendable. Keeping seven receivers on the roster never seemed likely.

The Texans, meanwhile, very much needed another option after the Higgins loss. Nico Collins will lead the passing attack but there aren't many trustworthy options behind him, with the oft-injured Tank Dell, second-year man Jaylin Noel and Xavier Hutchinson the main options in that regard. The team did sign veterans Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones on Friday, however, and Boutte will be expected to carve out a role for himself as well.

Given C.J. Stroud's struggles last season, an uninspiring group of receivers behind Collins and one of the NFL's best defenses, it wouldn't be surprising if the Texans relied heavily on the running back duo of David Montgomery and Woody Marks, hoping to control time of possession and grind out wins.

But when they do need to open up the passing game, adding Boutte should benefit the effort.

articles.title: Patriots send WR Kayshon Boutte to the Texans for S Jaylen Reed, draft pick
articles.summary: The Texans have found their replacement for injured WR Jayden Higgins.
articles.body:
The Patriots have traded WR Kayshon Boutte to the Houston Texans for safety Jaylen Reed and a draft pick, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero .

The move helps clear up some space in what had become a crowded receiver room in New England , while also giving the Texans some added depth at the position.

Boutte, 24, settled into a solid complementary role over the past two seasons with the Patriots, catching a combined 76 passes for 1,140 yards and 9 TDs in 29 games (23 starts). In last season's playoffs, Boutte led the Patriots with 168 receiving yards in four postseason games.

It's understandable why Boutte would want to go elsewhere this season. With the Patriots signing Romeo Doubs and trading for A.J. Brown , it left Boutte's role in doubt. The Patriots still have Mack Hollins back, and there are two other young receivers on the roster, DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams , who could be in line for more snaps and production volume.

There was speculation in June, after the Brown trade was official following months of anticipation, that Boutte could have quietly let New England know that he wouldn't mind playing elsewhere in 2026 .

This is a crucial season for Boutte. The former sixth-round draft pick is entering a contract year, set to hit free agency in the spring, and now appears to have a better chance to increase his market value with a big season in Houston vs. a more crowded New England depth chart.

The move comes on the heels of Texans wide receiver Jayden Higgins tearing his ACL during training camp. He was ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 season.

Boutte was used primarily as a perimeter threat in the past two seasons and was effective on vertical shots, but he was also used occasionally in the slot. His production peaked in the first half of last season, before a hamstring injury that reemerged in the postseason, despite some strong playoff moments.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson Browns timeline: Inside disastrous trade, contract that brought quarterback to Cleveland
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson's tenure with the Browns has not gone well.
articles.body:
The 2026 Cleveland Browns engaged in the most depressing position battle of the summer to ultimately choose Deshaun Watson . The once-superstar talent has had a rough go of it since joining the franchise in 2022, but will get one more opportunity to prove himself.

There are — thanks to the many things Watson has said and done over the past couple years — legitimate questions about that decision. The Browns seemed to realize as much last year, drafting not one, but two possible quarterbacks of the future in the 2025 NFL Draft. Despite their presence on the roster, Watson won the job yet again.

Given the various ups and downs Watson has experienced across his career, it's worth re-evaluating how the Browns got to this point.

April 27, 2017: Texans select Deshaun Watson in NFL Draft

After a standout college career at Clemson, Watson entered the NFL Draft as one of the top prospects available . While he was the third quarterback taken off the board — Mitchell Trubisky and Patrick Mahomes went higher — Watson didn't have to wait long. The Texans took him with the No. 12 overall pick in the draft, presumably giving the team a quarterback of the future after Brock Osweiler started 14 games for the team the previous season.

Sept. 14, 2017: Deshaun Watson makes his first NFL start

It didn't take long for the Texans to throw Watson into the starting lineup. After the team benched Tom Savage at halftime in Week 1, Watson made his NFL debut, throwing a touchdown and an interception to close out the loss.

The following week, the team decided to stick with Watson under center. He led the team to a 13-9 win in his first-ever start, rushing for a score in the victory.

Nov. 2, 2017: Deshaun Watson tears ACL to end promising rookie season

Watson only made five more starts for the Texans that season. During a November practice, Watson tore his ACL , missing the rest of the season. He finished with 19 passing touchdowns against eight interceptions. Despite only playing in seven games, Watson finished third in the Rookie of the Year voting.

Sept. 5, 2020: Deshaun Watson signs extension with Texans

Watson returned from his ACL injury and blossomed into a superstar with the Texans. Fresh off two straight Pro Bowl seasons, the Texans agreed to pick up Watson's fifth-year option.

But before the start of the 2020 NFL season, the team signed Watson to a four-year, $156 million extension . It solidified his future with the franchise.

Watson responded by going out and throwing for a league-high 4,823 yards and a career-high 33 touchdowns. The Texans, however, went just 4-12.

Jan. 28, 2021: Deshaun Watson demands trade from Texans

Frustration with the state of the team and the front office led to Watson demanding a trade from the Texans. The franchise did not seem interested in honoring that request.

Mar. 17, 2021: Deshaun Watson accused of sexual misconduct

A lawsuit emerged accusing Watson of going "too far" while getting a massage from a female masseuse.

Rumors of the lawsuit came to light a day earlier, leading to Watson issuing a preemptive statement claiming has has "never treated any woman with anything other than the utmost respect."

April 5, 2021: Twenty-two different women join sexual misconduct lawsuit against Deshaun Watson

In less than a month, a number of accusers filed lawsuits against Watson. That number grew to 22 on April 5, leading to the Texans to finally issue a statement .

In the coming days , all but one woman gave up anonymity to proceed with the lawsuits against Watson.

April 19, 2021: Deshaun Watson says all 22 women are lying

Watson's attorney issues a statement claiming all 22 women to file suit against the quarterback are lying .

April 30, 2021: Texans take Davis Mills in 2021 NFL Draft

With both the trade and the off-the-field allegations swirling, the Texans selected Davis Mills in the third round of the 2021 NFL Draft. While Mills wasn't a high pick, the selection seemed to hint at the Texans worrying Watson wouldn't be around, either due to a trade or a suspension from the NFL, which had started performing its own investigation.

July 25, 2021: Deshaun Watson reports to Texans training camp

With all those issues still unresolved, Watson reported to training camp in July. The Texans now seemed willing to trade the quarterback, who had not been placed on the NFL's commissioner exempt list yet.

Jan. 9, 2022: Deshaun Watson does not play 2021 season with Texans

The Texans played their final regular-season game Jan. 9, finishing the season 4-13. Despite never being placed on the commissioner's exempt list, Watson didn't play a single down of football for the Texans during the 2021 season.

Mar. 11, 2022: Grand jury declines to indict Deshaun Watson on criminal charges

A Houston grand jury did not find enough evidence to indict Watson of a criminal act . Watson still faced civil lawsuits and the NFL's investigation, but avoiding criminal charges gave the Texans a runway to ship Watson out.

Mar. 18, 2022: Deshaun Watson traded to Browns, signs record contract

Watson waived a no-trade clause to join the Browns. In exchange for Watson, Cleveland gave up three first-round picks, a third-round pick and a fourth-round pick. The team immediately signed Watson to a five-year, fully-guaranteed, $230 million contract . That fully-guaranteed figure remained the most in the NFL until 2025, when Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen exceeded it.

Aug. 18, 2022: NFL suspends Deshaun Watson 11 games, fines him $5 million

After spending the summer settling lawsuits , Watson received an 11-game suspension from the NFL .

That suspension put him out until Week 13, when he would face his former franchise, the Texans, in his first game since the 2021 NFL season.

Dec. 4, 2022: Deshaun Watson makes first Browns start, finishes season

Watson returned from his suspension in time to start against the Texans. In his first Browns' start, Watson threw for just 131 yards and an interception in a 27-14 loss.

He started the team's remaining five games, but looked rusty, finishing the year with seven passing touchdowns against five interceptions.

Nov. 12, 2023: Deshaun Watson out for season with shoulder injury

Watson opened the 2023 NFL season as the Browns' starter and put up middling numbers in his first three games before missing time with a shoulder issue.

After struggling with the injury for a few weeks, Watson was eventually knocked out for the rest of the year during a Week 10 game against the Baltimore Ravens .

He finished the 2023 season with seven passing touchdowns and four interceptions in six games.

Oct. 20, 2024: Deshaun Watson again sustains season-ending injury

Watson again returned to start in 2024, but failed to put up strong numbers in seven starts before rupturing his Achilles against the Cincinnati Bengals . He finished the season with just five passing touchdowns and three interceptions. The Browns were among the worst offenses in the NFL at the time of Watson's injury.

Jan. 10, 2025: Deshaun Watson tears Achilles again

Watson experienced a setback and had to undergo yet another surgery on his Achilles tendon. The issue was expected to keep him out for potentially the entire 2025 NFL season .

Mar. 31, 2025: Browns co-owner Jimmy Haslam says Watson trade was a 'big swing and miss'

The Watson era in Cleveland appeared to be over, as co-owner Jimmy Haslam admitted the trade for the quarterback was a " big swing and miss ."

"We thought we had the quarterback; we didn't. And we gave up a lot of draft picks to get him, so we've got to dig ourselves out of that hole … [The trade] was an entire organization decision and it ends with Dee [Haslam] and I, so hold us accountable."

April 25, 2025: Browns select two quarterbacks in 2025 NFL Draft

Following multiple years of disappointing play and injuries from Watson, the Browns signal they are moving on, taking Dillon Gabriel and Shedeur Sanders in the 2025 NFL Draft. Neither are high picks, as Gabriel went in the third round and Sanders was taken in the fifth round .

Those two were expected to compete with veteran Joe Flacco early on.

Dec. 3, 2025: Deshaun Watson cleared to return to practice

Watson made enough progress in his recovery to be cleared to return to practice in December. The move came as Sanders was prepping to make his third NFL start.

Gabriel had started a handful of games with the team as well before an injury pushed him out of the starting role.

Jan. 4, 2026: Browns finish 2025 season 5-12

Though Watson made progress in his recovery, he was never activated from the PUP list and did not appear in a game with the 2025 Browns.

Sanders closed out the season as the team's starter, tossing seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in seven starts. It was enough to earn Sanders a Pro Bowl nod after multiple other players opted out of the event.

NFL news, live updates: Ja'Marr Chase 'fine' after 'little hyperextension' of his knee; Browns announce Deshaun Watson as starter over Shedeur Sanders

Sean McVay can't comprehend players going from NFL camps back to college: 'I feel like I took a freakin' gummy'

49ers owner Jed York reportedly contacted fictitious prostitution ad posted by police prior to arrest

April, 29. 2026: Deshaun Watson starts getting buzz in minicamp

With Watson back, the Browns opted to allow the veteran to compete for the starting job. Positive reports soon emerged, suggesting Watson was performing better than Sanders in minicamp.

Aug. 22, 2026: Deshaun Watson booed by Browns fans in preseason

In what was potentially a deciding game in the Browns' quarterback competition, Watson and Sanders put up middling numbers against the Buffalo Bills in a preseason 31-7 loss.

Watson's performance, however, drew more ire from fans, who booed him when he took the field and then booed him even more after a bad interception. Watson didn't take kindly to that treatment, saying it was personal and " disrespectful. "

Aug. 24, 2026: Deshaun Watson wins Browns' starting job, apologizes to fans

It's 2026 and, somehow, Watson has returned. The Browns officially named him the team's starter over Sanders on Monday.

The 2026 season will mark the final year of Watson's $230 million fully guaranteed contract. Heading into 2026, here's how he's performed with the Browns since the trade:

In Watson's first public appearance since that news, he apologized for the way he handled Saturday's game, saying his emotions got the best of him.

Watson, who hasn't thrown a pass in an NFL game since 2024, will open the year under center when the Browns travel to play the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1. The Browns will also play their Week 2 game on the road before Watson returns to Cleveland to take on the Carolina Panthers at home in Week 3.

Barring a fantastic start to the season, Watson may not receive the warmest response from Browns fans when — or if — he takes the field for that game.

articles.title: Matt LaFleur Jokes He'll Fight Brother Mike During Packers-Cardinals Joint Practice
articles.summary: Fights have run rampant during NFL joint practices over the past few weeks, and Matt LaFleur is ready for anything as the Green Bay Packers have a joint practice with the Arizona Cardinals.
articles.body:
Fights have run rampant during NFL joint practices over the past few weeks, and Matt LaFleur is ready for anything as the Green Bay Packers have a joint practice with the Arizona Cardinals.

He joked that he'll fight his brother, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur, if it comes to it.

"If there's an issue, I'm going to tell the guys, 'Hey, you come tag me in. They can tag in my brother. And we'll throw down on the 50,'" Matt LaFleur told reporters Monday.

🎥 Pickens' Trash Talk from Joint Practice

Those comments didn't go unnoticed by Mike:

Matt LaFleur is entering his eighth season as the head coach of the Packers, while Mike LaFleur will make his head coaching debut for the Cardinals this season. Matt will, of course, look to pick up a win against his brother in a preseason game on Friday, but he also said he'll be cheering Mike on this year.

"I think it's going to be pretty special, but at the end of the day, we're just looking to try to get good work on both sides," Matt said. "Certainly, always going to prioritize the Green Bay Packers but if there is another team in the National Football League that I'll be rooting for, it will be the Arizona Cardinals."

The Packers have made the playoffs in all but one season since Matt LaFleur took over. Mike LaFleur, who spent the last three seasons as the offensive coordinator of the Los Angeles Rams, is hoping to find similar success in his new role.

articles.title: Updated Patriots, Texans WR Depth Charts After Kayshon Boutte Trade amid Fantasy Football Drafts
articles.summary: With Jayden Higgins out for the season because of a torn ACL, the Houston Texans reportedly continued bolstering their wide receiver depth Monday.
articles.body:
With Jayden Higgins out for the season because of a torn ACL , the Houston Texans reportedly continued bolstering their wide receiver depth Monday.

Tom Pelissero of the Ringer reported the Texans sent safety Jaylen Reed and a draft pick to the New England Patriots in exchange for Kayshon Boutte. This comes after Houston added both Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones.

Here is a look at the wide receiver depth charts for both teams after the move:

Fantasy Football Sleepers Getting Buzz 🐝

LWR: Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Jared Wayne, Zay Jones

RWR: Kayshon Boutte, Tank Dell, Justin Watson

SWR: Jaylin Noel, Lewis Bond, Sterling Shepard

LWR: A.J. Brown, Kyle Williams, Cameron Dorner

RWR: Romeo Doubs, Mack Hollins, Kyle Dixon

SWR: DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III, Nick DeGennaro

The trade bolsters Houston's overall ceiling in its race for an AFC South title and from a fantasy perspective.

After all, there were plenty of question marks about the room following Higgins' injury. Tank Dell hasn't played since the 2024 campaign, and Nico Collins was the only wide receiver on the team last season to finish with more than 525 receiving yards.

In fact, Higgins was second in that category, which meant it remained very much up in the air who would be the No. 2 option outside of Collins.

Enter Boutte, who had a career-high six touchdown catches last season and a combined 1,149 receiving yards the last two years. While he isn't someone who is realistically going to challenge for 1,000-plus yards in 2026, he is a proven option who should be able to fully capitalize on the double teams that Collins will surely draw.

That also makes him more valuable from a fantasy perspective than he would have been in New England this season after the reigning AFC champions added both A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs to the room.

Boutte likely would have been the third option at best, and that's not even including tight end Hunter Henry.

That Boutte was moved does not come as a surprise, as Karen Guregian of Mass Live reported he "requested a trade as far back as April." What's more, ESPN's Mike Reiss reported earlier this month he "would welcome a trade if the right situation presented itself."

It did present itself, and Boutte appears ready to take over the No. 2 role in Houston's offense alongside Collins. That also gives Dell a bit more time to work his way back into form after being away so long.

If everything goes according to plan, C.J. Stroud could have three game-changing wide receivers to work with this season following this trade.

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Sleepers Generating Buzz After Preseason Week 2
articles.summary: Fantasy football stocks move throughout draft season.
articles.body:
Fantasy football stocks move throughout draft season.

They might be most fluid, however, coming out of the 2026 preseason's Week 2.

With teams fielding the closest proximity to their actual lineup that we'll see in the regular season, there was valuable intel to be gleaned from noticing who took advantage of their opportunity and who did not.

With everyone chasing value propositions right now, let's find out which booming stocks are generating the right kind of noise.

The Packers are big fans of Matthew Golden. That was obvious as soon as they broke from their norm and spent a first-round pick on a wide receiver, taking Golden 23rd overall in last year's draft. It was evident again when Green Bay cleared out some of the obstacles around this summer, trading Dontayvion Wicks and letting Romeo Doubbs walk in free agency.

Golden appears to be rewarding that faith. While his rookie season was quiet, he ended it on a high note, tallying four receptions (on five targets) for 84 yards and a score in the Wild Card Round. And his lone target of the preseason could not have gone any better, as he snared a 19-yard pass from Jordan Love on a 4th-and-1 while beating lockdown corner Patrick Surtain II in the process.

"I think he has elite hands," coach Matt LaFleur told reporters . "That catch he made in Denver on the crossing route that kind of showed to it. It was a good savviness by him, he felt an underneath defender and he bled up the field. I think it was a good ball especially because he changed the angle on Jordan. But to make that catch and not lose stride, a low hands catch, I think that speaks to just how good his hands really are."

The Packers are clearly counting on a sophomore leap from Golden, and they'll give him every opportunity to help make that happen.

After suffering an ankle fracture back in January, Bo Nix carried a lot of question marks into his preseason debut. Would he be limited by the ailment? Would rust be obvious?

Well, so far, so really good. Nix, who might be a real bargain at his average draft cost of QB15 (per FantasyPros), was 6-of-9 passing for 76 yards and a touchdown. He connected on a 35-yard catch-and-run with notable newcomer Jaylen Waddle and a 21-yard touchdown pass to RJ Harvey.

""I felt like it (was) exactly where I left off," Nix told reporters . "I felt better. ... I felt pretty good, as good as I've felt in a long time."

Through two NFL seasons, Nix has racked up 7,706 passing yards with 54 touchdowns against 23 interceptions, plus another 786 yards and nine scores on the ground. If he is feeling good, this aerial attack could really hum, especially with that Waddle addition.

De'Zhaun Stribling, WR, San Francisco 49ers

It's obviously still early, but De'Zhaun Stribling keeps sending signals that he'll be the rare rookie receiver to handle a heavy-usage role for Kyle Shanahan.

Stribling's name has been buzzing throughout camp, and Week 2 only cranked up the volume. He hauled in four of his five targets (three from Brock Purdy) for 64 yards and ran routes all over the field.

"Obviously, really excited about him" Purdy said on The Pat McAfee Show recently. "He's a smart kid. He's come in, learned our offense. He's got strong hands, great route runner, all the things—the reasons why we drafted him. He's showing it and proving it."

With Ricky Pearsall lost for the season, George Kittle working his way back from a torn Achilles and the bulk of San Francisco's playmakers being on the wrong side of 30, Stribling has a real shot to be a featured part of this passing attack. His stock is rising, but it still isn't high enough (ADP: WR50 in PPR leagues).

articles.title: Malik Nabers' Injury Status Updated by Giants' John Harbaugh Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Malik Nabers is in the midst of an important week in his recovery from the torn ACL he suffered during the 2025 campaign.
articles.body:
Malik Nabers is in the midst of an important week in his recovery from the torn ACL he suffered during the 2025 campaign.

New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh told reporters Sunday the wide receiver could shed his no-contact jersey he's been practicing with as soon as this week.

"That's a possibility," Harbaugh said. "We'll just have to see where he's at."

He then provided another update Monday and said "it's reasonable to assume" Nabers could take the field in Week 1:

While the Giants don't take the field for the regular season until Sept. 13 when they face the rival Dallas Cowboys, they surely want their star receiver to have some practice time without the no-contact jersey before Week 1.

Nabers himself wouldn't commit to playing in Week 1 when he discussed how difficult the recovery process has been and instead took a long-term approach with his health:

"The most important thing is my health," Nabers said Monday. "The most important thing is just completing every milestone that they have in front of me, giving good effort, continuing to come out here and be a great teammate to my teammates."

At just 23 years old, a long-term approach is the correct one.

The Giants may be a year or two away from being legitimate contenders in the NFC East, and Nabers figures to be a major part of it as one of the best young receivers in the league. He posted 109 catches for 1,204 yards and seven touchdowns as a Pro Bowler in his rookie season in 2024 and was primed to build on that in his second season.

However, the torn ACL limited him to just four games in 2025 and has kept his health under the spotlight heading into the 2026 campaign.

Shedding the no-contact jersey is a key step back to make sure he can deal with tackles in the open field, and it seems like he is one step closer to a full comeback.

articles.title: Falcons HC Updates Tua-Michael Penix Jr. QB1 Battle, Can Preseason Star Jack Strand Win Job?
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons' quarterback battle is heating up with the Sept. 13 season opener approaching, and, no, it does not realistically include preseason star Jack Strand.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons' quarterback battle is heating up with the Sept. 13 season opener approaching, and, no, it does not realistically include preseason star Jack Strand.

On Monday, head coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters Michael Penix Jr. was cleared for all football activities as he recovers from the torn ACL he suffered last season. As a result, he will split first-team reps with Tua Tagovailoa.

"The new part for Mike is just being in there in with a full offensive line, a full defensive line, but he's been in walkthrough huddles, he's been in 7-on-7, he's obviously gone through individuals," Stefanski said. "So, this is a good—now that Mike is cleared—it's good that he can start that process of getting back to 11-on-11."

He added that he wouldn't speculate about whether Penix can start Week 1 but stressed, "everything we do around this building is competing."

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport also reported "this is Michael Penix's job for the taking."

Stefanski's comments come after Strand shined in the team's preseason win over the Indianapolis Colts. He went 12-of-17 for 212 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions.

The undrafted rookie drew some attention in the process:

Still, Stefanski said he will "work with the twos and threes" with Penix and Tagovailoa competing for the starting role.

There are plenty of concerns that come with both Tagovailoa and Penix. The former threw a career-high 15 interceptions last season after he was limited to just 11 games in 2024. He looked nothing like the Pro Bowl version of himself who led the league with 4,624 passing yards in 2023.

As for Penix, he is coming off the serious injury after also dealing with serious knee injuries in college. He is just 4-8 in 12 career starts since Atlanta selected him with the No. 8 overall pick of the 2024 NFL draft and hasn't been able to work in full this offseason prior to being cleared.

The Falcons have just one preseason game remaining Friday against the Miami Dolphins, so perhaps Penix can make an impression during live-game action much like Strand did against the Colts.

articles.title: Browns Making Another QB Error? 7 Takeaways From Week 2 Of The Preseason
articles.summary: Here's what we learned from this week's preseason games.
articles.body: Two weeks of preseason games are in the books, and we're starting to see the light at the end of the tunnel.  This past week's slate of preseason games, plus joint practices, brought us more glimpses of what we could expect to see in the regular season. But it brought some drama, too. Deshaun Watson was named the Cleveland Browns' starting quarterback on Monday after making pointed remarks to the team's fans following his lackluster performance on Saturday. There's also an unusual storyline developing with players who might wind up playing college football in the next couple of weeks.  So, with only one more preseason week to go, here are our takeaways from the latest slate of preseason games.  1. Deshaun Watson Didn’t Deserve The Starting Job In Cleveland. He Got It Anyway. Ralph Vacchiano: Deshaun Watson showed everyone on Saturday why he shouldn’t be the Cleveland Browns' starting quarterback, with a terrible on-field performance and an even worse one off the field. Then, Todd Monken gave him the job anyway.  Maybe that’s a sign that the new Browns coach had nothing but bad options in his quarterback competition, but his choice still couldn’t have been any worse. He went with a 30-year-old who’ll surely be an ex-Brown next season over a somewhat promising young quarterback, Shedeur Sanders. And he did it two days after Watson was terrible in a preseason game against the Bills (5 of 12 for 36 yards and an interception) and then showed an incredible lack of self-awareness (and an abundance of immaturity) when he whined about being booed. "I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do with the performance," Watson said. "It’s a little more personal than that. So, I think that’s a disrespectful thing." OK, that’s a little rich and a lot outrageous, coming from the man who got the biggest fully-guaranteed contract in NFL history from the Browns in 2022 (five years, $230 million) even though he hadn’t played in two years and was accused of sexual misconduct by 27 women. He then rewarded that startling generosity by only being healthy enough to play in 19 games over the last four seasons — and not particularly well, either. Even without that bad moment, though, Monken still made the wrong choice. The coach had been leaning this way, multiple team sources told me, in part because the Browns’ early schedule is overloaded with road games (their first two and six of their first nine), and Monken thought Watson’s veteran presence would help his young team. But Watson’s play didn’t warrant that faith. He was just 16 of 27 for 162 yards and an interception in two preseason games. His passer rating of 61.0 was even a notch below Sanders’ 65.2. So while it’s true that there was no good option here, it’s also true that really is no upside to Watson, who is understandably reviled by what seems to be a majority of the Browns’ fan base. Starting Sanders at least would’ve given them hope that he can get better, something to look forward to other than the QB-rich 2027 draft. Instead, Monken latched on to the anchor that has been scraping the Browns along rock bottom for the last five years. Sanders will surely get a shot later this season. But as usual in Cleveland, any hope for the future is delayed. 2. Yes, The Pipeline To The Pros Goes Both Ways Greg Auman: The most backwards trend of the NFL preseason? Marginal players testing the waters of playing in NFL preseason games and  … going back to college. It seems impossible, but these days, if you can get a judge to rule the right way, traditional lines of amateurism and eligibility can disappear. The NCAA’s shift to a five-year eligibility model wasn’t intended to be backdated for athletes who had exhausted their window – and signed a pro contract, gotten paid and even played for NFL teams. But that’s really happening, leaving general managers to wonder if they’ll lose players off their roster to the allure of NIL money from colleges. Tight end Dae’Quan Wright, an undrafted rookie with the Browns, put his name in the transfer portal. Cleveland has since waived him, setting him up to play for LSU this fall. "Man, ain’t this s--- crazy?" Browns coach Todd Monken said. "I mean, I don’t even know what to say … I wondered why Lane Kiffin reached out a week ago. Now I know. I didn’t call him back, guess I should have." Speaking of LSU, consider Tampa Bay Buccaneers undrafted rookie linebacker Jack Pyburn, who had two sacks in Tampa Bay’s preseason opener. He’s also one of the players granted a temporary restraining order that could allow him to return to college football. He played at LSU last year, and that sets up the man-bites-dog possibility of an NFL player leaving early for college. The fall semester at LSU started on Monday, and NFL rosters will be cut from 90 players to 53 by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday. It’s unlikely the Bucs will keep Pyburn for their 53, but he has (had?) a good shot at their practice squad. That pays $247,500 for a full season, and Pyburn could make three or four times that much on the Van Wilder go-back-to-college route. Pyburn said after Saturday’s preseason game that his agents had told the Bucs that college was a potential "backup plan," but when pressed as to what he might decide if choosing between an NFL practice squad and going back to college, he was noncommittal. "Ultimately, that’s a decision I’m going to have to make with my family, talk to my agents and see what’s the best business decision and what’s the best option for me and my future career," he said. Yes, it’s NFL "respect my decision" season. Players would have to repay their NFL employers to regain college eligibility. Pyburn got a $15,000 bonus and $100,000 in guaranteed salary, but it’s possible that college NIL payments could also be covered by "offset" language standard in such contracts, normally intended so if NFL Team B pays a player to be on their practice squad, that subtracts from the money NFL Team A was on the hook for by their guarantee. The league will have to sort out the ramifications. Can a player already passed over once in the draft get another shot, like baseball players do? This was already happening with basketball and G League players showing up on college rosters, but for NFL teams, it’s made roster-building even more complicated by the idea that players can make more money playing football at a lower level. 3. Stetson Bennett Commands Offense, Cements Role As Rams' Backup QB Eric D. Williams: With Jimmy Garoppolo no longer on the roster, Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay’s search for someone to fill that void, should reigning MVP Matthew Stafford suffer an injury during the regular season, appears to be over. In the battle between Ty Simpson and Stetson Bennett, the Alabama product cracked the door open with a sparkling performance in a Week 1 preseason win over the Kansas City Chiefs. But Bennett may have closed the door by playing well in a 34-0 victory over the New Orleans Saints at SoFi Stadium. The Georgia product finished with two rushing touchdowns in the first half, leading the Rams to scoring drives on four of his five possessions. Bennett finished 19 of 31 for 181 yards, with no touchdown passes and no interceptions for a 77.5 passer rating.  Ty Simpson also played solidly, finishing 8 of 12 for 73 yards in the second half. Simpson led the offense on one scoring drive. However, Bennett impressed McVay by the way he led the offense, with quarterbacks coach and associated offensive coordinator Dave Ragone calling the plays – although he didn’t like Bennett reaching for the pylon with the ball on his first rushing touchdown. "I loved the fact that he used his legs," McVay said. "We’ll learn from reaching the ball into the end zone, even though I challenged that and we were successful. We don’t want to leave ourselves susceptible to losing the ball out of the end zone where it goes for a touchback. "But he did a great job. I thought he got an opportunity to really showcase a lot of his skills." 4. Daniel Jones Primed To Pick Up From Where He Left Off Last Season Ben Arthur: Watching the Indianapolis Colts quarterback at Wednesday’s joint practice with the Atlanta Falcons, it was impossible for me to tell that he tore his Achilles just eight months ago. Everything you want your passer to do — drop back, scramble, throw on the move, evade pressure — Jones looked normal in doing so. Oh, and he was carving up the Falcons’ secondary as well. With Indianapolis’ rushing attack struggling, Jones was near perfect in the pass game, targeting various receivers.  We still need to see Jones move and perform in games. But all the early signs suggest that he can pick up from last season, when he was playing the best ball of his career before a broken leg slowed him down and the Achilles injury ended his season.  "I think with any major rehab process, you're always kind of progressing and getting back and getting used to doing everything, building up the reps on it, building up just your conditioning level," Jones said Wednesday. "I feel really good and there's nothing I don't feel good doing." The Colts’ pass-catching situation around Jones is a bit shaky at the moment, given star tight end Tyler Warren (groin) and wide receiver Alec Pierce (offseason ankle surgery) are currently sidelined. But when they return, they’ll add to a group that features one of the league’s best slot receivers in Josh Downs and recent signee Keenan Allen, who’s been a dominant force on third down.  That’s a cast of receivers Jones can find success with.  "I think it could be really special, to be honest," Colts coach Shane Steichen said of the pass-catching group. "Alec (Pierce) obviously is a hell of a football player, which you guys know. [Josh] Downs, Tyler [Warren], and then adding Keenan [Allen] to the fold. I think we can do a lot with those guys and move bodies around and find matchups."  5. Let’s Have A Conversation About Chiefs Breakout Rookie WR Cyrus Allen Henry McKenna: If you’ve been following training camp for Kansas City, you’ve heard of Allen. If you’re the type who combs X for potential breakout stars in fantasy football, you’ve heard of Allen. If you’re obsessed with NFL rookies and the draft, you’ve heard of Allen.  His training camp highlights have been crazy. And Andy Reid didn’t slow the hype’s momentum. "He's done a nice job," Reid said of Allen. "The quarterback trusts him." This was the first week of training camp. Allen was a sixth-round pick out of Louisiana Tech. It felt like a big proclamation, particularly given that Rashee Rice has a history of missing time due to injuries and suspensions and Xavier Worthy has failed to live up to his first-round hype.  Since then, Allen has played well — steadily doing what he could to move up the depth chart. That included scoring touchdowns with the first-team when paired with Patrick Mahomes. That also included beating first-round cornerback Mansoor Delane in 1-on-1s and team drills (7x7 and 11x11), per reporters on the scene. But here’s the truth for anyone expecting the second coming of Tyreek Hill. The folks at Arrowhead Pride broke it down with depth. But it’s likely — perhaps even overly optimistic — to project 60 for Allen. And only six receivers converted 60 targets into 500+ receiving yards in 2025. But before he wows in the box score, he’ll need to land in the WR3 spot. Given that he was playing behind Tyquan Thornton and Jaylen Royals in the second preseason game, Allen appears to be WR5. For what it’s worth, Hill had 83 targets, 61 catches, 593 yards and six touchdowns in his rookie season. That would be a great year for Allen. So keep an eye on him. He’s a real playmaker. But let’s stay reasonable for a rookie in a Chiefs' offense that has a lot of mouths to feed. 6. De’Zhaun Stribling Shows Kyle Shanahan Knows How To Evaluate WRs Williams: NFL draft analysts were up in arms over the San Francisco 49ers taking Ole Miss product De’Zhaun Stribling in the second round, believing the organization had reached for a player that some consensus draft boards had going later in the draft. However, through two weeks of preseason play, Stribling has acquitted himself nicely. Stribling is tied for the league lead with 11 catches for 109 yards, with a long of 32 yards. He finished with four catches for 46 yards in a win over the Los Angeles Chargers this week.  I had a chance to watch Stribling in a joint practice at the Chargers’ facility. At 6-2 and 210 pounds, Stribling is an easy mover with suction-cup hands that can make contested catches in congested areas. Along with that, Stribling has the potential for explosive playmaking ability to do something after the catch, a key attribute in Shanahan’s offense. With Ricky Pearsall out for the year and Brandon Ayiuk no longer on the roster, Stribling should find a significant role in San Francisco’s offense this season. "I love how he handles himself," Shanahan said about Stribling. "He takes coaching well and never seems to take anything personally. He’s been a real fun guy to coach so far." 7. Bills’ Thin WR Corps May Be More Of A Problem Than Ever Vacchiano: One great NFL mystery of this generation will surely be why the Buffalo Bills, with arguably the best quarterback in the league in Josh Allen, keep failing to surround him with top-end receivers. And once again, heading towards a season they hope will end in a Super Bowl, that failure is being exposed. Though they are getting a solid performance this summer from D.J. Moore, the veteran "No. 1" wideout they acquired from the Chicago Bears, the rest of the corps is falling apart. Keon Coleman, their second-best receiver last season (38 receptions for 404 yards and four touchdowns), is nursing a concerning sprained toe. Khalil Shakir, last season’s top wideout (72 receptions for 719 yards and four touchdowns), missed the joint practices and preseason game against the Browns last week with an undisclosed injury. And rookie Skyler Bell, their fourth-round pick, has missed two weeks with a groin injury. That leaves Allen right now with Moore, who cost the Bills a second-round pick in March, Joshua Palmer (22 receptions for 303 yards and zero touchdowns) last season, and … not much else. That, of course, is not how the Bills see it. One team source told me their belief is that Allen can win with almost anyone around him, and that he can take what looks like a below-average group and make them much better. They are also convinced that Moore, at age 29, can reverse his steep, two-year decline simply by playing with an elite quarterback. It’s a gamble, of course, because otherwise all the pieces are in place in Buffalo: A powerful running game led by James Cook, a top offensive line, a top-10 defense that gets a boost from the addition of edge rusher Bradley Chubb. And of course, the brilliance of Allen will always give them a shot. Still, it’s hard not to imagine what this team would look like with just one elite receiver by Allen’s side. It would make their path to Buffalo’s first Super Bowl in 33 years look a lot easier than it currently is.

articles.title: Cowboys HC Hypes Joe Milton's Growth, Says NFL QBs Are More Than 'Carnival' Arm Strength
articles.summary: When Joe Milton was drafted in 2024, the quarterback was known mostly for his cannon of an arm and not much else.
articles.body:
When Joe Milton was drafted in 2024, the quarterback was known mostly for his cannon of an arm and not much else.

Now, Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer believes Milton is more than just his arm. Schottenheimer told reporters Monday that Milton has grown tremendously ahead of the 2026 campaign.

"I first remember hearing about Joe Milton when he was at the University of Michigan and everyone applauded him for how hard and how far he could throw the ball. Cool. That's awesome. Go be in a carnival somewhere. That's not what playing an NFL quarterback is. It's not. … You're throwing through small windows, you're throwing over people, you're changing arm slots. So to me, arm strength is cool. Go to the fair and win a teddy bear. But you got to play quarterback. And that's what I think you see Joe learning is he's playing quarterback. And he's playing quarterback at a high level. He's checking the ball down. He's making blitz adjustments. He's solving problems. He's reading from his first, second to third, and even fourth progression at times. It takes time. You don't stop learning as a quarterback. The only way to do it is to play. I'm really, really proud of him."

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

During his time at Tennessee, Milton showed flashes of an NFL-starting quarterback but mostly relied on his arm and athleticism to make plays rather than making adjustments on the fly and going through his progressions.

He's played well in preseason this year, throwing for 107 yards and a touchdown on 12-of-15 passing against the Seahawks before recording 179 yards and two touchdowns on 9-of-13 passing against the Cardinals.

If all goes according to plan for the Cowboys this year, Dak Prescott will avoid injury and Milton won't see much playing time. But if he does have to take over under center, it sounds like Schottenheimer will have plenty of faith in him.

articles.title: New Aaron Donald Rumors on Contract Being Hold Up for Rams Return, DT Won't 'Play for Free'
articles.summary: Speculation about whether Aaron Donald will come back for the Los Angeles Rams has continued throughout the summer, and there still isn't a resolution.
articles.body:
Speculation about whether Aaron Donald will come back for the Los Angeles Rams has continued throughout the summer, and there still isn't a resolution.

During a Monday an appearance on The Rich Eisen Show (35-second mark), Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer reported the money aspect of the situation could be playing a role.

"This isn't from Rams people or from Donald's people, but one thing that has continually come up when I talk to other people in the league about it is, 'how do you work out the money part of it? How much are you paying him? How does it fit into their budget, both cash and cap?' So there's that piece of it too. I don't think he's going to want to come out there and play for free."

Still, the Rams have surely thought about the money part since speculation began that Donald would be coming back shortly after they traded for Myles Garrett.

With that as the backdrop, Breer suggested the financial component isn't the most important one.

"I think the bigger piece, and this is just me talking, is him feeling comfortable that he can go out there and be Aaron Donald," he said.. "… The trouble with that is it's not just his ability to play football at a high level. It's to be Aaron Donald."

Playing like peak Aaron Donald is a significant amount to ask of any player in NFL history.

The future Hall of Famer is 35 years old and hasn't played an NFL game since the 2023 campaign. He may remain dominant, especially playing alongside Garrett, but expecting him to be the same version of himself who put together a legendary resume is a bit unrealistic.

After all, that resume includes a Super Bowl title, three Defensive Player of the Year awards, a Defensive Rookie of the Year, eight First-Team All-Pro nods and 10 Pro Bowl selections. He led the NFL with 20.5 sacks in 2018 and has 111 for his career.

Breer reported the Rams will have a plan for him if and when he does return that will include a limited snap count to maximize his effectiveness.

Even if he isn't quite as effective as he was when he was arguably the best player in the league, he will surely be a difference-maker for the defense. First, though, he has to officially decide whether he will come back in 2026.

articles.title: Allen Robinson II Retires From NFL After 11 Seasons, Former Pro Bowl WR Played for Bears, More
articles.summary: Allen Robinson II is calling it a career.
articles.body:
Allen Robinson II is calling it a career.

The former Pro Bowl wide receiver announced his retirement on Instagram on Monday after an 11-season career with five teams.

Robinson was drafted in the second round in 2014 after a tremendous collegiate career with Penn State and spent his first four seasons with the Jacksonville Jaguars.

He had a standout second season in the NFL, racking up 1,400 receiving yards and 14 touchdowns, a number that led the league that year. He was named to his only Pro Bowl in 2015.

Unfortunately, in 2017, his career was derailed a bit when he suffered a torn ACL after just one game. That injury ended his time in Jacksonville, as he signed with the Chicago Bears ahead of the 2018 campaign.

Robinson managed to get back on track following the injury, putting together back-to-back seasons with 1,000-plus receiving yards in 2019 and 2020. After those two campaigns, his numbers started to taper off a bit.

He played for the Los Angeles Rams in 2022, the Pittsburgh Steelers in 2023 and rounded things out with the Detroit Lions in 2024.

Robinson campaigned for a spot on an NFL roster last year, specifically with the Kansas City Chiefs, but he ultimately went unsigned for the entirety of the 2025 season.

He told Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press last offseason that he was weighing retirement.

"I wanted to look back and have no regrets," Robinson said. "And that's kind of where I'm at with it is that I don't have (any). I've put everything I've had into this game."

Now, Robinson will head into retirement having put together a strong career that lasted more than a decade. He finished his time in the NFL with 7,058 receiving yards on 565 receptions with 43 touchdowns.

articles.body: For Kelli Finglass, leading the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders has never been only about flawless routines and game-day glamour. Her role has placed her at the center of auditions, tough decisions, television scrutiny and the changing pressures faced by young performers. As Netflixâs Americaâs Sweethearts returns for season three, Finglass is reflecting on criticism, motherhood, vulnerability and the possibility of eventually stepping away.Kelli Finglass on Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders and social media criticismKelli Finglass knows exactly what it takes to become a Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader because she once stood where the dancers now stand. She performed for the Cowboys from 1984 to 1989 before taking over as coach in 1991. Her career has since become closely tied to the evolution of the organization on television.The Netflix series has brought unprecedented attention to the cheerleaders, but that visibility has a downside. Social media criticism can follow the women beyond the dance studio, something Finglass says she has seen affect members of the team.She does not make a habit of reading online comments herself. Still, she understands the emotional weight they can carry.âThe words of people, while they can be very, very uplifting... Like in my personal case with my skin cancer journey, the people that reached out to me were extremely supportive," she said in an interview with Vanity Fair."Words can hurt and they can also heal. Iâm trusting humanity to help figure this one out because itâs a much bigger thing than I can solve. But the girls being busy and focused and supportive of each other is where our strength will remain.âThat outlook reflects a major lesson Finglass has learned through years of television. The cheerleaders do not need to appear perfect all the time.Kelli Finglass reveals her future with the Dallas Cowboys CheerleadersFinglass has also reconsidered what leadership means as she has grown older. She says motherhood changed how she sees the young women she coaches and helped her understand the struggles they face away from performances.Her approach has shifted from demanding perfection toward encouraging honesty and resilience.âI spent practically my whole career trying to create flawless performances, and what weâve learned through TV is that vulnerability is actually more attractive. People love when they can relate to somebody, and thatâs been an unexpected âahaâ for meâfor these girls to not project perfection, but rather be honest about their victories and honest about their struggles, has, I hope, given viewers something to find hope in and find something they can relate to.âNow entering her 35th season with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, retirement is no longer an impossible thought. Finglass says her family could ultimately influence that decision, especially as she looks toward becoming a grandmother someday.âI have, but weâre so busy, we donât have time to think about anything except the next hour. It would be a personal decision. Iâve sacrificed a lot of time with my family. My daughter is married, my son is in a relationship, and when I ever get the honor to be a grandmaâ¦I want that time if and when I have grandchildren. That would definitely give me a heartfelt reason to go to a new chapter.âFor now, Finglass remains focused on the next generation. articles.title: Texas Police Reveal No Criminal Findings and Close Case into Death of Bills' DT Ed Oliver's Son
articles.summary: BUFFALO, N.Y. (AP) — A police investigation into the death of Buffalo Bills defensive tackle Ed Oliver's 1-year-old son has resulted in no criminal findings and the case is now considered closed, the Harris County Sheriff's Office in Texas announced on Monday.
articles.body:
BUFFALO, N.Y. (AP) — A police investigation into the death of Buffalo Bills defensive tackle Ed Oliver's 1-year-old son has resulted in no criminal findings and the case is now considered closed, the Harris County Sheriff's Office in Texas announced on Monday.

The closing of the case comes after the child's death on June 28 was first confirmed on Saturday in a statement from Bills GM Brandon Beane expressing condolences to Oliver .

Police say the toddler, who was a few days shy of his second birthday, was found unresponsive in the swimming pool of a home in a neighborhood community just north of Houston. The boy was transported to the hospital where he was pronounced dead.

"The incident was thoroughly investigated by detectives, and their finding were no criminal findings. The case is now closed," the police statement said.

Oliver has asked for privacy and prayers while still mourning his son, who was also named Ed.

"Obviously, very unfortunate what happened and as a teammate of him, as someone in this locker room, all we can do is love on him," quarterback Josh Allen said following Buffalo's 31-7 preseason win at Cleveland on Saturday .

"There's nothing that you can say to make the situation any better except being there in whatever ways he needs," Allen added. "I can't imagine what he's going through. But the way that he's dealt with it has been unbelievable."

The 28-year-old Oliver is entering his eighth NFL season since being selected by Buffalo in the first round of the 2019 draft out of Houston. He has been with the team since reporting for the start of training camp.

Oliver appeared with the starters in the Bills' preseason-opening 29-14 win over Carolina, but has missed the past week of practice due to an undisclosed injury.

CLEVELAND (AP) — The Buffalo Bills are giving defensive tackle Ed Oliver support and space following the accidental death of his 1-year-old son.

Oliver has been grieving throughout training camp and many of his teammates only learned of the tragic accident on Friday. Following Saturday's 31-7 preseason win over the Browns , Bills quarterback Josh Allen said the team is standing with Oliver.

"Obviously, very unfortunate what happened and as a teammate of him, as someone in this locker room, all we can do is love on him," Allen said. "There's nothing that you can say to make the situation any better except being there in whatever ways he needs.

"That's what we're going to continue to do. That's what teammates do. You love up on each other when we're down, and I can't imagine what he's going through. But the way that he's dealt with it has been unbelievable."

Oliver has asked for privacy and prayers while still mourning his son, who was also named Ed. The toddler was pronounced dead after being found unresponsive in a residential pool in Harris County, Texas, on June 28, a person briefed on what happened told The Associated Press. The person spoke to the AP on the condition of anonymity because the team and player have not revealed that information.

Without providing many details including names or ages, the Harris County Sheriff's department posted a note on its Facebook account that evening regarding the drowning of a toddler in a neighborhood community north of Houston.

"This is a tragic incident and our thoughts are with the toddler's family during this incredibly difficult time. The investigation is ongoing," the post read.

A sheriff's official told The Associated Press on Saturday that a report was not immediately available.

Before Saturday's game, Bills general manager Brandon Beane issued a statement expressing his and the organization's condolences.

"It's an unthinkable tragedy for any parent. We will continue to support Ed and his family as we grieve this tragic loss," Beane said .

Bills first-year coach Joe Brady was equally compassionate toward Oliver, who is in his eighth season with Buffalo.

"Ever since I found out the news, I can't fathom what he's going through," Brady said. "As a coach and a father, there really aren't words to describe it. It's all about us loving him and giving him the privacy that he deserves.

"It's hard when I see him. I don't have the words, but all I can do is support him in whatever way he needs."

The 28-year-old Oliver was selected by the Bills in the first round of the 2019 draft out of Houston.

Oliver reported for training camp on time last month and appeared with the starters in the Bills' preseason-opening 29-14 win over Carolina last weekend. He has not practiced this week because of an undisclosed injury.

This story has been corrected. A previous version, relying on information provided at the time by police in Harris County, Texas, reported that Oliver's son was 2 years old when he died. Police subsequently reported that the boy was 1 year old.
