articles.title: Deshaun Watson beating Shedeur Sanders as Browns' Week 1 starter is just the beginning. Now, a tenuous reality awaits
articles.summary: Multiple sources with knowledge of the Browns' decision-making factors suggest: The decision to name Watson rather than Sanders did not arrive via a landslid...
articles.body:
When Deshaun Watson booed the boos that rained down from fans on Saturday , the Cleveland Browns quarterback questioned not only his fan base's actions but also their intentions.

"I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do with the performance," Watson told reporters after the 31-7 loss.

The line left plenty to unpack about the history between quarterback and fan base. It also seemed to gain further relevance Monday when the Browns named Watson their starting quarterback for their season opener. Because while Watson (accurately or not) believed fans' boos had "nothing to do with the performance," Cleveland's decision to name Watson its Week 1 starter has plenty to do with it. If the Browns' decision was about fan popularity or podium performance or medium- to long-term upside, 2025 fifth-round pick Shedeur Sanders would have received the nod Monday.

Play Yahoo's new College Fantasy Football game: Create or join a league now!

Instead, a conversation about who gives the club its best chance to beat the Jacksonville Jaguars in Jacksonville on Sept. 13 unfolded.

"You don't ignore the fans and the tax that maybe something like that can put on the organization, but we also have to make football decisions," a person with knowledge of the Browns' decision-making factors told Yahoo Sports. "You also can't be emotionally hijacked and not make what you think is the sound, right football decision."

Multiple sources with knowledge of the Browns' decision-making factors suggest: The decision to name Watson rather than Sanders did not arrive via a landslide. This was not a decision about who is "good" or "bad" and perhaps not a decision about who is the better or worse NFL quarterback.

"I do think there's maybe a little bit of an element here in terms of what you value in terms of their relative strengths and weaknesses," a second person with knowledge of the Browns' decision-making factors told Yahoo Sports. "Deshaun's athletic. You'll have the operation right. He's really good pre-snap. Shedeur, he's accurate. He's very, very poised in the pocket. He's a good drop-back passer and he can create enough off schedule with his legs, but you're not going to do QB designed run."

Monken opted to promote the player with 72 career starts whom he believes is superior in nuances like the silent count required on the road, rather than the seven-start player whose quarterbacking skills may deserve the edge.

Watson's strengths — which are different from those of Sanders, whether or not they are better — won out.

That tenuous reality was clear even as Monken sandwiched a "this is not a week-to-week decision" comment between his notes that Watson is going to start "against Jacksonville" and "ultimately, we're about Week 1."

How much cushion does Watson have and what would prompt consideration for an eventual change?

Those are questions the Browns must ask themselves even before their season officially starts.

Monken made clear on Sunday that he understands what's expected as he fielded questions about Watson's emotional outburst.

"The business we're in is a performance-based business," Monken told reporters. "It is what it is. When we expect a service, we're going to be disappointed when we don't get that service. If you go to a restaurant and your soup comes out cold, you're going to be upset. If you order from the grocery store and six of your eggs are broken, you're going to be pissed. So, I get it, that's what we're in. That's why we're paid what we are, to perform at a high level, and when we don't, there are repercussions. We've run to this smoke.

"This is the job we've chosen, so this is part of it."

After rocky weekend, what does Watson's starting role mean?

For a stretch over the weekend, there was reason to wonder if Watson had forfeited the starting right that his offseason and training camp performance had narrowly earned him.

Insulting a fan base is rarely a winning strategy in professional sports. Insulting a fan base as a player years removed from strong performances and winning is still dicier. Watson's apology on Monday , after he was named the Browns' Week 1 starter, might resonate with some. His background facing allegations of sexual assault and misconduct, and the multiple injuries he's suffered while costing three first-round draft picks in a 2022 trade and a $230 million fully guaranteed contract, make him generally unsympathetic to others.

But Watson's Monday opening statement struck a different tone than he's had since arriving in Cleveland.

"My emotions got the best of me," Watson admitted of his Saturday comments in which he called Browns fans booing a "disrespectful" gesture. "I'm human. I take full responsibility of that. Moving forward, I want to make sure I put the best product out there for the team."

He noted also that "I understand the frustration" from fans watching a losing product and believes winning will help him "earn the respect and loyalty of the rest of the fan base."

#Browns Deshaun Watson apologizes for his postgame remarks, saying he’s human. Wants to win for the fans: pic.twitter.com/LXbIvkPgdO — Mary Kay Cabot (@MaryKayCabot) August 24, 2026

#Browns Deshaun Watson apologizes for his postgame remarks, saying he’s human. Wants to win for the fans: pic.twitter.com/LXbIvkPgdO

Watson's actions must echo and then speak louder than his words in the coming weeks. But in the short term, perhaps they send a message to Cleveland's locker room that the club's quarterback realizes his comments were a mistake.

Perhaps that was the point, if not the best possible outcome of Watson's mea culpa. Did a large subsection of fans shift their core beliefs because their quarterback made a 2 1/2-minute statement? Unlikely. But did a locker room and coaching staff far higher on Watson than their fan base perhaps receive some reassurance that his lost-cool comments won't become a norm? That's more plausible.

Earning back some grace from colleagues after this weekend would be wise. Because not only did Sanders rise above the news conference drama Watson created, but Sanders also played better than Watson in the last benchmark of the decision that ultimately wasn't close enough to close the gap in the competition. Evaluators say snaps with each phase of the roster matter. But when trying to predict Week 1 performance, each quarterback's snaps with the starters ultimately prove most representative.

Thus Watson's preseason Week 1 stat line of 11-of-15 passing for 126 yards and a lost fumble ultimately became a part of his win relative to Sanders' Week 2 showing of 9-for-11 passing for 74 yards, a touchdown and an interception (plenty of caveats exist for each performance amid a preseason atmosphere and in-flux roster).

Watson's early Cleveland games paled in comparison to his Houston Texans tenure, as his completion percentage dropped from 67.8% in Houston to 61.2% in 19 Cleveland games across three years. His production went from 269.2 passing yards per game in Houston to 177.1. Add in Achilles tears that will separate his last start and his next by 693 days, and questions abound.

But Watson is optimistic that teaming up with Monken will unlock some of his strengths that haven't flashed recently.

"We haven't showcased my full talent and ability to run in this offense, being able to run and being able to use my athletic ability, getting outside the pocket, being able to do some other QB-driven stuff," Watson said. "So, I'm excited to see what we can cook up getting ready for Week 1."

Why Watson's starting nod doesn't spell Sanders' end with Browns

Browns decision-makers stressed on Monday: Giving Watson the early nod does not mean they've given up on Sanders.

No one's saying publicly or directly that Sanders is likely to start later in the year. But consider Cleveland's history of quarterback carousels and its two first-round picks looming in 2027: If Sanders is healthy all year, it will be a surprise if he doesn't receive a start.

"Shedeur has improved a ton," the first source with knowledge of the Browns' decision-making process said, echoing Monken's public sentiments. "You can argue where he's coming from, fine, but he's improved a lot. And he still could not be the better one. Or could not be the one that's right. I don't know why both can't be true.

"Because the other guy is more ready or is the right choice, in our minds, doesn't mean Shedeur sucks. Both things can be true. It could just be, 'Hey, this is the right decision for us right now.'"

Watson's performance Week 1 at Jacksonville and Week 2 at Tampa Bay — against his predecessor in former Browns' first overall pick Baker Mayfield , no less — will dictate what's the right decision for the Browns afterward.

Yes, Cleveland opening at home Week 3 amid their famously unsupportive-of-Watson crowd will factor into a decision. Maybe early wins will win Watson some favor with the fans. Maybe the need to build a young roster will become more pressing. Could Sanders end up starting Week 3 through the rest of the season and demonstrate how much he's advanced from a year ago? That's plausible. If that happens, will the Browns regret not rolling with him Week 1?

"It's not actually that simple with the variables," Monken said in explaining the quarterback decision to Yahoo Sports on Aug. 7. "A number of players, when it's that close, you don't know for sure. You think you know. But you know what? At some point, you put Lamar Jackson in the first time. They didn't know, and at first, they probably thought he couldn't do what he's done.

"And then he developed at it, and he got better."

The Browns will need to decide what factors will most dictate their roster battles as the season progresses. How will Monken and Co. react if the team is 2-0 but their offense is ineffective, or if they are 0-2 but Watson has played well? How about if the Browns return home at 1-1, with an average Watson and an average offense — but also a young talent in Sanders whom at least some in the building believe could approach quality starter level?

Why Sean Payton ordered a life-sized cardboard cutout of OC Davis Webb to Broncos camp

After chippy Broncos practice sends Bo Nix to ground, Denver reminds defense its goal is to be 'smart bullies'

From Fred Warner cautioning Cam Ward to De'Zhaun Stribling unsatisfied, 5 takeaways from San Francisco 49ers camp

At some point, the medium- to long-term future of the position will creep into decisions about the short-term future. And there's a reality in which this gives Sanders his best chance of the season.

Because unlike Watson, starting Week 1 on the road with multiple receivers who haven't played an NFL game and a play-caller in Monken still adapting to his personnel, the insertion of Sanders later in the season could position him to enter an offense that has more intel on what it needs most and how it can best succeed.

The Browns expect Sanders to stay engaged until that moment arrives, the younger quarterback aware that his next start in Cleveland is a matter of when not if under a staff that sees his potential even if noting it's rawer than that of Watson.

"Ultimately, we felt over the course of training camp and the offseason that [Watson] was ahead of Shedeur," Monken told reporters on Monday. "Shedeur has closed that gap, for sure, and that's a credit to him. …

"We met this morning for a good long time, and all he had was a smile on his face, because he understands what's really in front of him: not really a short-term, more of a long-term decision.

"This is a player who's going to work his butt off to get better, and he already has."

articles.body: BENGALURU: As the state moved to the next phase of special intensive revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls, Monday, with the claims and notice period, draft SIR rolls already had 1.07 cr of Karnatakaâs 5.5 cr voters axed as they were on the ASDDO category.That number was frozen on Aug 17 night. Now, the election commission will now work with just 4.4 cr voters who are on the draft rolls. Of these, at least 4.02 crore will make it to the final list of Oct 27 as they are not due for notices.Of the 4.4 cr voters on the draft list, the remainder 43.81 lakh voters are due to receive notices and have to furnish documents, and upon verification, they too can be added to the final rolls that will be published Oct 27.Bengaluru emerged as the biggest hotspot for SIR voter verification as 46.88 lakh of its 1.03 cr voters left out of the draft rolls. articles.summary: Jed York pleaded no contest to two charges in Ohio after being arrested for soliciting prostitution.
articles.body:
Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York has been jailed in Ohio after being arrested for soliciting prostitution.

The 45-year-old, who is also the owner of the San Francisco 49ers, was convicted of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools after pleading no contest to two charges.

In the Ohio legal system, a no contest plea means a defendant accepts a conviction without formally admitting guilt.

York was sentenced to one day in jail on each offence, to be served concurrently, and was given credit for time already served.

York was fined $150 for disorderly conduct and $1,000 for possessing criminal tools.

Court records show the case was brought by East Palestine Police Department and filed at Columbiana County Municipal Court on Monday.

York pleaded no contest to both charges at an arraignment hearing and was found guilty.

Court records also show an expungement request was filed and denied on the same day. This is a request to have records destroyed or sealed so they are not accessible to the public.

According to reports in the US media, other court documents say York responded to an advertisement on a prostitution website placed by undercover officers from a Human Trafficking Task Force in Ohio.

These documents say he arranged to have sexual activity with a woman in exchange for $140 (£103).

In a plea deal, the original charge was reduced to disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools - thought to refer to the phone used to reply to the advert.

The 49ers were part of the US consortium who took control of Rangers last year but York is not involved in the day-to-day running of the club.

Rangers and Leeds have both said they will not be commenting.

The 49ers said: "As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time."

York became a co-owner of Rangers through 49ers Enterprises, the investment arm linked to the NFL's San Francisco 49ers, where he serves as chief executive and principal owner.

In May 2025, a consortium led by US businessman Andrew Cavenagh and 49ers Enterprises completed a takeover of Rangers after acquiring a controlling 51% stake in the Scottish Premiership club.

Cavenagh became Rangers chairman, with 49ers Enterprises taking a leading role in the club's ownership.

The takeover followed months of negotiations and brought Rangers under majority American-backed ownership.

49ers Enterprises first invested in Leeds United in 2018 when the club was in the Championship, steadily increasing its investment as the Whites returned to the Premier League following a 16-year absence, before assuming full control in 2023.

As an NFL owner, York is subject to league policies. "We are aware of the matter which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy," the NFL said.

articles.title: NFL Players for Fantasy Managers To Target in Trades Before 2026 Roster Cuts
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL season is just over two weeks away, and the Patriots and Seahawks will soon meet in Seattle for a Super Bowl LX rematch.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season is just over two weeks away, and the Patriots and Seahawks will soon meet in Seattle for a Super Bowl LX rematch.

With the regular season approaching, fantasy football draft season is in full swing, as managers prepare for drafts in person and online.

However, even as draft season accelerates, some fantasy managers—particularly those in dynasty leagues—will look to improve their rosters through trades.

Trading can be tricky, especially in redraft leagues. Managers are often reluctant to make a deal if they believe they may be giving up too much, which can lead to inflated asking prices or stalled negotiations. Still, opportunities emerge when another manager is willing to move the right player for a fair return.

You can make low-ball offers for Jahmyr Gibbs all day long—it's not going to happen. But if you know who to target, you can add a player who can help your chances at fantasy glory without breaking the bank.

While there has been quite a bit of player valuation movement at the other positions, the quarterback market has been pretty stagnant—the pecking order now is essentially what it was three months ago.

Given that, what fantasy managers looking for an upgrade need is a signal-caller who is productive and has some long-term upside but doesn't carry a lofty price tag.

Jared Goff of the Detroit Lions fits the bill—and then some.

Goff was second in the league in passing yards and sixth at the position in fantasy points a year ago. Fantasy Football World co-host Brian Johnson said recently that Goff's fantasy ceiling is a fair bit higher than that.

"The lack of mobility will hurt him, but I think Jared Goff still has a shot to finish as QB1 overall", Johnson said. "The Lions did lose their starting center, Cade Mays. That hurts, but (that might mean) maybe more shotgun (while Mays is out) for Goff, who has elite weapons in Amon-Ra St. Brown, we know that, but who's to say Jameson Williams is not the top wide receiver for the Lions this year? We're just looking at shootouts galore for the Lions, who have 11 of their final 13 games in a dome. Their defense is dog water. They have the easiest schedule in the NFL. I just think they're slinging it all day, every week."

The top quarterback overall may be a stretch. But Goff hasn't finished lower than QB7 over the past three years. At 31 years old, Goff is still relatively young by quarterback standards. He's at the helm of one of the NFL's best offenses.

And on as many teams as not, Goff is rostered as a backup.

Finding a reasonably priced running back upgrade on the trade market can be difficult, as fantasy managers often place a premium on the position.

However, Javonte Williams could be available at a more manageable price. He is coming off a career year, though his production declined over the second half of the season. It was the first standout campaign of his career, and his injury history may further temper his trade value.

However, per Derek Brown of Fantasy Pros , Williams' per-game metrics show a back who has the potential to be a viable fantasy starter for the next few years.

"In Weeks 1-8, he had a 4.8% explosive run rate with an 11% missed tackle rate and 3.52 yards after contact per attempt," Brown said. "That yards after contact per attempt mark is otherworldly. In Weeks 8-17, he posted a 5.5% explosive run rate with a 13% missed tackle rate and 2.33 yards after contact per attempt. He improved his marks down the stretch in two of those three categories. If Williams can post production as he did over the first half of the 2025 season for an entire year, he is a locked-in top ten back with top-five upside. At his floor, he looks like a low-end RB1 or top 15 fantasy back."

You'll probably want to leave that stuff out when you send the trade offer, and Williams isn't going to be cheap.

But among short-term upgrades available at a reasonable cost, he is one of the strongest options.

There isn't a backfield in the NFL that inspires less confidence among fantasy managers this year than the two-headed attack of Aaron Jones Sr. and Jordan Mason.

However, that lack of hoopla could be a blessing in disguise if it means that Mason could be available for a reasonable cost in a trade. Because as Mike Barner wrote for 4For4 , there's upside to be had with the fifth-year veteran.

"Mason gains yards in chunks," he said. "When he was given his first significant workload as a member of the 49ers in 2024, he averaged 5.2 yards over 153 carries. That included nine carries of at least 20 yards. The Vikings gave him a similar workload last season, and he averaged 4.8 yards over 159 rushing attempts. He had a broken tackle rate of 20.1% that contributed to his averaging 3.1 yards after contact. That outproduced teammate Aaron Jones, who had a 9.1% broken tackle rate and averaged 2.5 yards after contact."

Yes, the presence of Jones caps Mason's fantasy ceiling in the short-term at least. Mason also isn't a big factor in the passing game. But Jones will turn 32 in December, he has missed at least five games in two of the past three seasons and his contract is up after the 2026 season.

There is also a path for Mason to become Minnesota's lead back in 2027, which could make him an attainable trade target now.

WR Marvin Harrison Jr., Arizona Cardinals

Trading in fantasy football is admittedly a speculative affair. Sometimes you need to be willing to roll the dice on a player who hasn't met expectations to this point in his career.

A player like Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr.

After a so-so rookie season, Harrison's second year in the pros was a mess—five missed games, 41 catches and 608 receiving yards. Harrison also made news earlier this offseason with some drops on the practice field, although the youngster told reporters that he's not going to let getting roasted on social media get to him.

"It's easy to look at the results," he said. "I know whether if I don't make a play that someone thinks I should have made, they're going to post it, and it's going to do what it's going to do in the social media era. And that's OK. For me, it's just I'm worried about my process, know what I do each and every single day to prepare myself for practice, prepare myself for games on Sunday. And what the result's going to be, the result's going to be. But I know Monday through Saturday, I'm going to do the best I can to make sure I put my best foot forward."

At this point, more than a few fantasy pundits are essentially willing to write Harrison off—and if pundits are doing it, fantasy managers are as well.

Harrison was the fourth overall pick in the 2024 draft for a reason. He was considered by some the best overall prospect in his draft class.

Over four professional seasons, Christian Watson of the Green Bay Packers has been one of the most frustrating wideouts in fantasy football.

The flashes have been there, but Watson just hasn't been able to stay on the field—he has missed at least three games in every season, including seven missed contests in 2025.

But the Packers had enough confidence in Watson to give him a four-year, $110.5 million extension, and per Shane Hallam of Draft Sharks , his advanced stats should inspire confidence in the 27-year-old as well.

"In his age-26 season," Hallam said, "Watson quietly led Packers WRs in targets per route and yards per route. Among the 76 WRs who drew at least 50 targets last season, he ranked 24th in the former and fifth in the latter, trailing only Puka Nacua, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Luther Burden and Zay Flowers. According to Pro Football Focus, Watson's 2.51 yards per route was a career high, but he'd already shown strength in that area. He tied for 14th in that category in 2024 among 84 WRs with 50+ targets."

The Packers thinned out a crowded wide receiver room this offseason—Dontayvion Wicks and Romeo Doubs are gone now. A healthy Watson should serve as Green Bay's No. 1 wide receiver this year. And his fantasy ceiling is far higher than most wideouts available at his price point.

The manager with Watson rostered may be frustrated by his injury history and willing to consider a trade. That creates an opportunity to acquire a talented receiver whose upside could exceed his current price.

There are pitfalls that even the most seasoned dynasty managers fall into. One of the biggest is "future lock." They become so fixated on the long-term prospects of their franchise that they pass on the chance to add the sort of short-term fix that can turn a contender into a champion.

Teams that are in that "win now" window and need an upgrade at tight end should make a run at Travis Kelce of the Kansas City Chiefs.

Kelce's 2025 campaign was nowhere near his best—his 50.1 receiving yards per game was the lowest output in that regard of his career. But even in that "down" year Kelce finished third in PPR points among tight ends, and with Patrick Mahomes expected back for Week 1, Jamey Eisenberg of CBS Sports expects Kelce to once again be a big part of Kansas City's offense.

"As long as Mahomes is ready to play in Week 1," he said, "that connection should still be strong, and Kelce was solid in 2025 in 14 games with Mahomes. During that span, Kelce averaged 12.8 PPR points, and the only tight ends who finished better than that were Trey McBride, George Kittle, Brock Bowers and Tucker Kraft. Given the cost, Kelce is worth the risk, and he didn't postpone retirement to not be a key player in another potential Kansas City Super Bowl run."

Kelce last finished outside the top five at his position in his second NFL season, in 2014. Given his age and uncertain long-term outlook, managers who are not positioned to contend could be willing to move him now rather than risk losing value later.

Gary Davenport is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow Gary on X at @IDPGodfather .

articles.title: NFL: At least one in four dead players had brain disease, says study
articles.summary: A new study says at least one in four ex-NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had a degenerative brain disease but the true figure could be much higher.
articles.body:
As many as 97.7% of NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 could have had brain disease related to repeated blows to the head, a new study says.

Researchers looked at 878 former players who died during that period, with 235 having donated their brains to research.

Of those, 215 were found to have chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a degenerative brain disease which can only be diagnosed after death.

The study, published in the British Medical Journal , external , also found dementia was common among brain donors.

"We and others have shown that in NFL players, specifically, there is about a four times higher rate of death from neurodegenerative disease than the general population," said the report's lead author Daniel Daneshvar, an associate professor at Harvard Medical School.

"These findings indicate that NFL players have a higher prevalence of CTE at death than has been previously shown in multiple community based studies."

Researchers calculated a "conservative minimum" of CTE prevalence among those who died in the six-year period to be 24.5% - rising to a "maximum" 97.7%.

They have urged the NFL to take prevention measures to reduce repetitive head impacts across all levels of the sport.

Dallas Cowboys player who died by suicide diagnosed with brain disease Published 8 July

Dallas Cowboys player who died by suicide diagnosed with brain disease

NFL admits football-brain disease link Published 15 March 2016

New research finds link between head impacts & CTE Published 27 July 2022

New research finds link between head impacts & CTE

"The bulk of the head impacts that these former NFL players experienced didn't occur at the NFL level," Danshvar said.

"They occurred at the collegiate level and at the high school level and in many cases the youth level. And all of those cumulative hits to the head added up to result in an increased risk."

An NFL spokesperson said: "The NFL continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts.

"The NFL remains committed to ensuring that the NFL community has access to a robust - and expanding - set of resources to enhance their physical and mental well being.

"We encourage former players to utilise these resources to identify and seek treatment when they are concerned about their health."

CTE among American football players has been a growing issue in recent years. A 2011 Collective Bargaining Agreement for the NFL limited the number of contact practices.

Following a long-running class action, in 2016 the NFL agreed a $1bn (£700m) settlement with more than 5,000 former players.

articles.title: New Report Concludes At Least 24.5% of NFL Players in Study Had CTE
articles.summary: A new study examining the brains of deceased former NFL players found that at least 24.5 percent of players in its cohort had CTE, a degenerative brain disease.
articles.body:
A new study examining the brains of deceased former NFL players found that at least 24.5 percent of players in its cohort had CTE, a degenerative brain disease.

The study, published by The BMJ , examined the brains of 235 of the 878 former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021. Researchers found 215 of the analyzed brains had chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), leading them to the conclusion that at least 24.5 percent of all players who died in that period had CTE.

According to ESPN : "The estimate of 25% is on the 'low end,' said Dr. Daniel Daneshvar, the study's lead author. The study found that the maximum possible prevalence of CTE was around 97%, but the true rate 'is somewhere in the middle,' Daneshvar said."

More broadly, the study incorporated the 1,712 NFL players who died between 2008 and 2021. It found that of 338 former NFL players who donated their brains to be studied for neuropathological evaluation, 315 (93.2 percent) were found to have CTE. The study's main conclusions focused on 2016-2021 because brain donation was most frequent in that period.

Boston University wrote in 2023 that a study of 376 former NFL players showed 345 of them were found to have CTE.

The disease is likely caused by repeated head injuries, leading to the death of nerve cells in the brain. There is currently no way to definitively diagnose CTE in a living person.

Former NFL quarterback Matt Hasselbeck was part of a group that recently went through a series of tests and scans at Boston University that researchers hope will eventually help lead to the ability to diagnose CTE in a living person.

articles.title: Top Potential Trade Packages and Landing Spots for Steelers' Joey Porter Jr.
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers and Joey Porter Jr. could be heading for a breakup.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers and Joey Porter Jr. could be heading for a breakup.

Last week, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that the cornerback has been seen as a "potential trade target" for teams as he enters the final year of his rookie deal and has yet to receive a contract extension from the Steelers.

Head coach Mike McCarthy stopped short of ruling Porter out for Week 1.

Asked whether he needs to see the 26-year-old—who has missed all of training camp with a back injury—practice before clearing him to play, McCarthy instead pointed to the "impasse" between the team and its top corner, according to ESPN's Brooke Pryor .

Porter has maintained his desire to be compensated as a top-level corner, a position that has seen five players reach or eclipse the $30 million per year mark since the start of last offseason, including a record-setting four-year, $133 million contract for Seattle Seahawks star Devon Witherspoon.

While Porter probably won't reset the market, he's due for a major raise over the $4 million in base salary he's due in 2026. The corner has been a lynchpin in Pittsburgh's secondary since being drafted No. 32 overall in 2023. In that span, he has appeared in 41 games—starting 41—and recorded 165 tackles, 31 pass defenses and three interceptions.

Because the Steelers have a longstanding organizational policy to not negotiate contracts during the regular season, time is running out for Porter and the club to hammer out a new deal.

If the two sides can't reach a fair agreement—which Spotrac pegs to be in the range of $23-24 million annually, although likely to run a good bit higher when the corner eventually signs—before the team's 2026 NFL season-opener on September 13, it could lead to a shocking trade.

Although trading Porter away represents a worst-case scenario for the Steelers, far more shocking events have happened in the NFL. With that in mind, let's highlight some potential trade packages and landing spots for Porter.

Pittsburgh Steelers receive: 2027 second- and sixth-round draft picks

Chicago Bears receive: CB Joey Porter Jr.

The Chicago Bears go into the 2026 NFL season with hopes of building on a promising 11-6 campaign. Trading for Joey Porter Jr. would greatly assist in that endeavor, adding a top-flight corner to a roster that nearly reached the NFC Championship Game last year.

After ranking bottom-five in total defense and allowing a whopping 32 touchdowns through the air last year, Chicago brought in several veterans—including projected starter Coby Bryant—to reinforce the safety position.

While that should help shore up one of the weak points in the secondary, the club could still heavily benefit from adding a Pro Bowl-caliber corner.

The Bears do have one standout corner already in Jaylon Johnson, although he's maintained that 2026 is a contract year for him despite still having two seasons left on the four-year, $76 million deal he inked following a breakout 2023 campaign.

With Johnson's future with the organization uncertain, Chicago's brass could get ahead of a potential disastrous situation by acquiring Porter and locking him up on a long-term extension.

The rest of the cornerback room in the Windy City leaves something to be desired.

Tyrique Stevenson is serviceable when healthy but is now week-to-week with an injury . Rookie fourth-rounder Malik Muhammad II has potential to be an impact player, but is still a raw, developmental prospect.

Kyler Gordon's status is particularly concerning. Although he was a consistent starter for his first three years in the league, the 2022 second-rounder appeared in just three games last season and is set to open 2026 on the PUP list with a calf injury. It's an ailment that is reportedly frustrating the coaching staff and has led to a "standoff" per The Score's Matt Spiegel during an appearance on Fox 32 Chicago.

With so many question marks for this season and Johnson's status for 2027 and beyond already in doubt, Chicago should make the bold move to trade an upcoming second-round pick for Porter.

A starting cornerback tandem of Johnson and Porter would give the Bears a big leg up in what figures to be a brutally tough NFC North race, and the team needs all the help it can get if it wants to successfully defend its title.

Pittsburgh Steelers receive: 2027 second- and fifth-round draft picks

Green Bay Packers receive: CB Joey Porter Jr.

The Green Bay Packers are in the market for a new corner. According to Easton Butler of Packer Report, the club has inquired about the availability of several veteran defensive backs, a list that includes Kool-Aid McKinstry, Riley Moss and Joey Porter Jr.

Porter would be the splashiest acquisition Green Bay could make, but also the most impactful. He's a borderline Pro Bowler who can immediately slot into the starting lineup for an NFC North squad looking to make a leap in 2026 after back-to-back Wild Card round eliminations.

While Green Bay has a handful of solid veterans at the cornerback spot, none offer the same blend of age, upside and production that Porter provides.

The team's recent depth chart release showed Carrington Valentine and Keisean Nixon starting, with rookie second-rounder Brandon Cisse and Kitan Oladapo serving as backups. Porter represents a large upgrade and his presence alongside star safety Xavier McKinney would give the Packers one of the NFL's most formidable secondary units.

Nixon could potentially be included in a Porter trade as well, given that ESPN's Rob Demovsky called him the most likely candidate to be released or dealt if Green Bay opts for a "high-profile move on cutdown day."

Packaging him and a Day 2 pick would likely be enough to get Pittsburgh to move on from Porter if an extension can't be reached in the next few weeks.

Green Bay doesn't possess a first-rounder in the 2027 draft due to their blockbuster trade for Micah Parsons last year, but is sitting on a second-round selection and a pair of third-rounders.

There's enough capital here to get a deal done for Porter, who could be a long-term building block in Titletown by signing a long-term deal shortly after arriving.

Pittsburgh Steelers receive: 2027 third- and fourth-round draft picks

Miami Dolphins receive: CB Joey Porter Jr.

The Miami Dolphins are in the midst of a rebuild, but adding a star-caliber cornerback like Joey Porter Jr. could help expedite the process. The team is extremely thin in the secondary and is largely lacking impact veterans like Porter who could get the franchise trending in the right direction.

The 'Phins are set to head into the new season with 2025 fifth-rounder Jason Marshall Jr.—a backup on last year's squad—and JuJu Brents, another depth option who spent most of last season on IR, playing large roles alongside first-round rookie Chris Johnson.

The team has been shuffling the deck at the position throughout training camp, most recently parting ways with Nick McCloud and adding Ja'Onte' McMillan off waivers to bolster the position. It's clear that the team isn't satisfied with how the position is faring in the preseason, making a blockbuster trade for Porter a potential path forward.

While giving up draft picks, especially selections likely to fall towards the top of the order, isn't ideal for an organization that needs help at nearly every position, the opportunity to land a proven player of Porter's caliber may be too alluring to pass up.

New York Giants receive: CB Joey Porter Jr.

The New York Giants have had a transformational offseason and seem ready to emerge as a contender again after some lean years, but their cornerback position still appears to be a bit shaky.

Adding Joey Porter Jr. into the mix would massively improve the secondary and give Big Blue the elite defensive back it needs to contend with the talented NFC East wideouts it is set to come up against in 2026.

The G-Men head into the campaign with incumbent Paulson Adebo remaining a starter on the outside. He largely failed to live up to the three-year, $54 million deal he signed last offseason, earning a paltry 58.4 grade from Pro Football Focus for his lackluster efforts.

The prized free-agent pickup missed five games with injury and struggled when he was on the field—allowing a career-worst 66.3 percent completion rate in coverage .

Fellow veteran Greg Newsome II is projected to be New York's other starting outside corner, but there are legitimate concerns about his consistency after some up-and-down seasons. Rookie Colton Hood oozes potential and has flashed his upside during training camp, but tasking the inexperienced second-rounder with a large role this early could backfire.

Rather than hope Adebo and Newsome return to form and Hood comes out of the gate strong, the Giants could instead trade for Porter and instantly solidify the cornerback position.

Armed with a pair of Day 2 picks in the 2027 draft, the Giants could easily put a fair offer on the table for Porter's services. It's a bold move, but one New York shouldn't hesitate to make if it truly believes it's ready to return to Super Bowl contention under head coach John Harbaugh.

articles.summary: After Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty injured his ankle in practice on Sunday, many feared the worst.
articles.body:
After Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty injured his ankle in practice on Sunday, many feared the worst.

However, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported on Tuesday that Jeanty's outlook isn't so dire, as he avoided any kind of season-ending injury.

"It's nothing like that," Rapoport said. "My understanding... is that it's an ankle sprain believed to be more low than high, and not considered to be a major injury. But it is a real injury, and the reality is, there is a chance that Ashton Jeanty may not be on the field for Week 1. They are hopeful that he will be. There is a chance that he won't be."

Multiple reports sparked a wave of concern on Sunday when it was revealed that Jeanty had to leave practice early and could not put weight on his leg as he was helped off the field by trainers. ESPN's Ryan McFadden reported that the second-year back suffered the injury when he dove for a catch and landed awkwardly on his right leg during team drills, and his teammates "took a knee and said a prayer after Jeanty exited the field."

Jeanty is coming off a strong rookie season. He totaled 266 carries for 975 yards and five touchdowns while also adding 55 receptions for 346 yards and five more scores. The 2025 No. 6 pick was widely expected to make a leap in his sophomore campaign under first-year head coach Klint Kubiak, who was the offensive coordinator of the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.

While Jeanty's injury doesn't appear to be a long-term setback, the Raiders will likely be cautious with his recovery. Rapoport noted that his potential absence will allow Las Vegas to explore its running back depth, and "that might not be a bad thing, either." Rookie ball-carrier Mike Washington Jr., a fourth-round pick in this year's draft, has impressed with 119 yards across two preseason games.

Once Jeanty is back at full strength, the Raiders will give him the lion's share of the carries as they try to emerge from their ongoing rebuild.

articles.title: Why did the Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel scandal fade so quickly? NFL analyst questions the silence
articles.summary: NFL News: The Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel controversy made waves in April 2026 and then, almost without warning, stopped. Photographs reportedly showing the .
articles.body: The Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel controversy made waves in April 2026 and then, almost without warning, stopped. Photographs reportedly showing the former Athletic reporter and New England Patriots head coach together at a Sedona resort surfaced, Russini resigned following an internal review, and the NFL media largely moved on. Analyst Drew Boylhart does not think that silence was accidental. He believes the story was inconvenient for too many powerful people inside the league, and that is exactly why it disappeared.Why did the Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel scandal receive so little media coverage?Boylhart made his position clear on X, arguing that the NFL and its media partners had every reason to keep the story contained. "Notice how the NFL, with help from the media, has buried the Dianna Russini/Mike Vrabel scandal," he wrote. "Why, you ask? Because she knows all the players, owners, and coaches who are doing the same thing. WOKE Goodell doesn't want to open that Pandora's box."His argument is speculative, not evidential. But the underlying concern he raises is worth examining. Russini was not a fringe figure. She was a prominent NFL insider with access to coaches, front offices, and locker rooms. She voted in the Associated Press balloting for major awards including MVP and Coach of the Year. The ethical questions her situation raised about journalism, access, and proximity to power were real, regardless of what specifically happened between her and Vrabel.The Athletic did conduct an internal review. Russini resigned. The review was still ongoing at the time the story faded. Vrabel, after a brief absence, remained in his role with the Patriots. For something that touched on media ethics, journalistic integrity, and league accountability, the conversation moved on remarkably fast.Boylhart's read is that one high-profile investigation risked pulling back a curtain the league preferred to keep closed.What did Aaron Rodgers say about the NFL silence on the Dianna Russini scandal?Aaron Rodgers was one of the few prominent voices in the league who pushed back on the quiet. Appearing on The Pat McAfee Show, the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback was openly frustrated. "You have literally an individual that maybe used to work at ESPN that covers our league at the highest level, and there's a major scandal, and it's just like nobody can [Explicit] talk about it. What are we even doing here?" he said.Rodgers did not provide any new information. What he did was name the discomfort a lot of people seemed to be feeling but were not willing to say out loud. When an NFL quarterback is the loudest voice questioning media accountability, that says something about how thoroughly the story was avoided by those with more to lose.Whether Boylhart's specific theory holds weight or not, the broader pattern he points to is harder to dismiss. Russini's departure resolved the immediate situation. The questions it raised about access journalism in the NFL did not go away just because the news cycle moved on.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

On Monday, the Cleveland Browns named Deshaun Watson their starting quarterback over Shedeur Sanders, who will take the backup role.

One day later, Sanders' father, Colorado football coach and Pro Football Hall of Famer Deion Sanders, dropped a post on social media urging people not to dwell on the past.

It's unclear whether the post was in response to Sanders being named QB2, a general inspirational remark or a bit of both. Regardless, Shedeur is the backup for now, but head coach Todd Monken raved about Sanders' professional response after being told the news (h/t Irie Harris of cleveland.com).

"He was awesome. I mean, you talk about somebody that really understands the long game. That really, I think, has come to understand the long game. What are we really in this for? What am I in it for? To have the Browns be an organization that people aspire to be, right? The long game, right? Where do we want to be in the long term? He understands that as well as a quarterback. Where he was at, where he's at now, where he wants to get to. That is what's so awesome about Shedeur understanding that. Really, he does. We met this morning for a good long time, and all he had was a smile on his face because he understands what's really in front of him, not really a short-term, more of a long-term decision. I mean, this is a player who's going to work his butt off to get better, and he already has."

Sanders, who was the Browns' starter for the final seven games last season during his rookie year, will be QB2 when Cleveland opens 2026 on Sunday, Sept. 13 at the Jacksonville Jaguars. That certainly doesn't mean he'll be the backup forever, though, as the door can open down the road.

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Updated Rankings and Advice for Team Names
articles.summary: Opening kick of the 2026 NFL season is barely two weeks away.
articles.body:
Opening kick of the 2026 NFL season is barely two weeks away.

For fantasy football managers who haven't finalized their draft plans, what's the hold-up?

Well, maybe you're trying to extract as much information as possible before building that blueprint. So, you need to stay up-to-date on things like updated rankings and movement among fantasy stocks from two weeks of preseason action.

We're here to provide both, plus some bonus tips on how to craft the best team name.

Stock up: Jonathon Brooks, RB, Carolina Panthers

Stalled to this point by two ACL tears, Brooks might finally be healthy enough to make his mark. The 2024 second-round pick seized his opportunity Friday night with Carolina's starting group, tallying five carries for 18 yards and a score.

Meanwhile, his primary competitor for carries, Chuba Hubbard, was sidelined by a hamstring injury. Brooks might be the more dynamic option even if both are healthy, though, and he could be a great value pick in the eighth or ninth round.

Stock down: Tony Pollard, RB, Tennessee Titans

Fantasy fans of Pollard will flock to his volume potential. He has neared (and sometimes surpassed) 300 touches each of the past three seasons, and Tennessee might have to lean on its ground game if quarterback Cam Ward can't take a big step forward.

But what happens if Pollard is trapped in a timeshare? Because it kind of seems like the Titans want to up their usage of Tyjae Spears, who has slotted alongside their starters more often than Pollard this preseason. If Pollard is left fighting for touches, then he just isn't worth the draft cost ( RB30 , per FantasPros).

Stock up: De'Zhaun Stribling, WR, San Francisco 49ers

Stribling's stock hasn't seen a spike so much as it has perpetually climbed until now. His buzz was building in training camp, and he has kept it moving up with two impressive showings in as many preseason contests, turning 13 targets into 11 receptions for 109 yards.

With Mike Evans struggling to stay on the field, and George Kittle still working his way back from a torn Achilles, Stribling could have a path toward a sizable role in this passing attack. It looks like it might take a top-100 pick to get him, but every sign so far suggests he'll be worth it.

Fantasy managers become their own branding departments when it's time to name the team. Consider us your branding consultants, then, as we'll sift through some options.

If you want something simple that you can carry forward into future campaigns, you can always build the name around your actual name. It isn't the most clever play, but there are no questions about who's in charge of Tommy's Touchdowns or The Zach Attack.

Or maybe you like tailoring it to a standout player on your roster, perhaps your first-round pick. If you're fortunate enough to land Bijan Robinson, then you could use Bijan Mustard, To Infinity and Bijan or Bijan Frisé. Or if you take Christian McCaffrey, Run CMC is always a classic.

Finally, perhaps your prefer to flex some pop culture knowledge. Cleated Rivalry might be right up your alley, then. Or The Trojan Hurts works if you have Jalen Hurts on the roster and enjoyed The Odyssey .

articles.title: Hallan encefalopatía traumática en 25% de exjugadores muertos de la NFL
articles.summary: Golpes en la cabeza recibidos desde la etapa juvenil acumulan un efecto que termina por ser mortal en jugadores de fútbol americano, sugiere el estudio.
articles.body:
Según un estudio publicado el martes, se determinó que al menos uno de cada cuatro exjugadores de la NFL de fútbol americano fallecidos entre 2016 y 2021 padecía encefalopatía traumática crónica (ETC). De los 878 exjugadores que murieron en ese periodo, 235 donaron sus cerebros; los investigadores hallaron ETC en 215 de ellos. La ETC es una enfermedad degenerativa que solo puede diagnosticarse de manera definitiva tras la muerte .

Detrás de cada porcentaje hay historias de deportistas que dedicaron años a competir al máximo nivel. El estudio vuelve a poner el foco en una pregunta que ha perseguido al fútbol americano durante décadas: ¿cuál es el costo a largo plazo de los golpes repetidos en la cabeza ?

Un portavoz de la NFL declaró: "La NFL se esfuerza continuamente por hacer que el fútbol americano sea más seguro, incluso mediante la implementación de estrategias para reducir las conmociones cerebrales y los impactos en la cabeza.

" La NFL mantiene su compromiso de garantizar que la comunidad de la liga tenga acceso a un conjunto sólido —y en expansión— de recursos para mejorar su bienestar físico y mental.

"Animamos a los exjugadores a utilizar estos recursos para identificar problemas y buscar tratamiento cuando les preocupe su salud".

El autor principal del estudio, Daniel Daneshvar —jefe de medicina física y rehabilitación en Mass General Brigham y profesor asociado de la Facultad de Medicina de Harvard—, señaló que las lesiones cerebrales traumáticas recurrentes son un factor conocido en las elevadas tasas de enfermedades neurodegenerativas.

"Asimismo, nosotros y otros investigadores hemos demostrado que, específicamente entre los jugadores de la NFL, la tasa de mortalidad por enfermedades neurodegenerativas es unas cuatro veces mayor que en la población general", añadió.

El estudio, realizado por Mass General Brigham, la Universidad de Boston y la Concussion & CTE Foundation, también reveló que la demencia era frecuente entre los donantes de cerebro; por ello, los investigadores instaron a adoptar medidas preventivas centradas en reducir los impactos repetitivos en la cabeza en todos los niveles de este deporte.

"La mayor parte de los impactos en la cabeza que sufrieron estos exjugadores de la NFL no ocurrieron en el nivel profesional, sino en el universitario... y en el de secundaria, e incluso, en muchos casos, en categorías juveniles. Todos esos golpes acumulados en la cabeza se sumaron para dar lugar a un mayor riesgo", afirmó Daneshvar.

Uno de los hallazgos más llamativos es que el riesgo no se concentra únicamente en la élite deportiva. Según los investigadores, la exposición acumulada comienza años antes de llegar a la NFL, lo que amplía el debate sobre la seguridad de millones de jóvenes que practican este deporte.

El convenio colectivo de la NFL de 2011 limitó el número de entrenamientos con contacto durante la temporada. Cinco años más tarde, la Ivy League prohibió los placajes de contacto total durante los entrenamientos. La Corte Suprema allanó el camino para que la NFL concretara en 2016 el acuerdo de conciliación de las demandas relacionadas con las conmociones cerebrales presentadas por miles de jugadores retirados.

"Si los cambios implementados en la NFL —incluida la reducción de la cantidad de contacto en los entrenamientos a menos de una sesión por semana— se extendieran a los niveles universitario, de escuela secundaria y juvenil, los deportistas saldrían beneficiados", afirmó Daneshvar, quien instó a los atletas actuales y retirados que presenten síntomas cognitivos a buscar una evaluación por parte de un especialista en enfermedades neurodegenerativas. " Sabemos que casi el 70 % de los impactos en la cabeza se producen durante los entrenamientos . Por lo tanto, sin modificar ni un solo minuto de tiempo de juego en ninguno de esos niveles, podemos reducir considerablemente la carga acumulada de impactos en la cabeza que estas personas sufren a lo largo de su vida".

Mientras los investigadores insisten en que muchos de estos impactos pueden prevenirse, la discusión ya no gira únicamente en torno al rendimiento deportivo, sino al equilibrio entre la pasión por un deporte de contacto y la protección de la salud cerebral a largo plazo. ¿Hasta dónde deberían llegar los cambios para reducir ese riesgo?

articles.title: Bears, Lions, Packers, Vikings Reveal 'Rivalries' Uniforms for 2026 NFL Season in New Photos, Videos
articles.summary: The teams from the NFC North will be rocking some new threads for key showdowns throughout the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The teams from the NFC North will be rocking some new threads for key showdowns throughout the 2026 season.

Along with the four teams from the AFC South, the Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions, Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings unveiled their new "Rivalries" uniform designs through the "Nike x NFL Rivalries" program on Tuesday. Each team will debut its uniform during a home game against its division rival this year.

"Revealing eight new Rivalries uniforms marks the next chapter in a program that is beloved by fans across the NFL and Nike," Taryn Hutt, vice president of club marketing for the NFL, said in a statement, per Scott Thompson of Fox News. "By spotlighting the launch of the AFC South and NFC North Clubs and the passionate communities behind them, we continue to capture the spirit and tradition of football's greatest divisional rivalries."

The Packers will be the first to showcase their Rivalries uniforms when they face the Bears in Week 5. The Lions will follow in Week 8 against the Vikings, who will then show off their new threads against Detroit in Week 15. Chicago will rock the new uniforms in Week 16 against Green Bay.

The Rivalries uniforms will be added to each team's alternate jersey lineup for the next three years. The teams that had their Rivalries uniforms debut last year will also wear them at some point this season, and it can be expected that more teams will join the program in 2027 and 2028.

Unlike the traditional alternate uniforms all 32 teams will use in rotation, the rivalries look is being phased into the NFL over a period of four years. The NFC East and AFC West will get theirs in 2027, followed by the AFC North and NFC South in 2028.

The NFL will keep the rivalry uniforms in rotation for three years after their debut. So the AFC South will use these particular jerseys through the 2028 campaign.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers effect: Why a Steelers rookie says sharing the field with him sparks real anxiety
articles.summary: NFL News: Germie Bernard did not arrive at Pittsburgh expecting to feel nervous around his own quarterback. But the Steelers' second-round pick out of Alabama h.
articles.body: Germie Bernard did not arrive at Pittsburgh expecting to feel nervous around his own quarterback. But the Steelers' second-round pick out of Alabama has been refreshingly candid about the pressure of sharing a field with Aaron Rodgers, a 42-year-old playing his final NFL season and clearly not coasting through it. Bernard, selected 47th overall in the 2026 Draft, admitted during the preseason that Rodgers' presence alone puts him on edge in a way no opponent has managed to.Why does Aaron Rodgers make Steelers rookie Germie Bernard so nervous?It is not about fear. It is about wanting to meet the standard of someone who has set the bar impossibly high for over two decades. Bernard put it bluntly: "I'm not going to lie, I be having low-key a little bit of anxiety when I'm out there with him, just because I don't really want to mess up and he finna chew my aâ out."That is the Rodgers effect in plain language. Four MVP awards, a Hall of Fame trajectory, and a reputation for holding everyone around him accountable. For a rookie still learning NFL route timing and defensive tendencies, that kind of proximity to greatness is as motivating as it is terrifying.What makes Bernard's admission interesting is the balance underneath it. He is not complaining. He is not rattled to the point of dysfunction. He added: "At the same time, it's like I enjoy being there with him and being under him because he's just teaching me the game. He's giving me all the knowledge he knows about the game."That dynamic, anxiety sitting right next to gratitude, tells you a lot about how Rodgers is operating this season. Cameras caught him advising Bernard on the sideline during a recent preseason game. That is not the behavior of a quarterback mentally checked out in his final year. Rodgers is invested. He just demands the people around him be invested too.Bernard was productive at Alabama, but college success rarely comes with a guarantee. The NFL asks wider route trees, faster reads, and defenders who get paid specifically to stop you. Having Rodgers in his ear every day of this first season is the kind of football education most rookies never get.Pittsburgh's season likely hinges on whether Bernard and the other young receivers around Rodgers can create separation consistently enough to keep the offense moving. The Steelers fell to Houston in the Wild Card last year. Rodgers wants one more run at something meaningful before he leaves.Bernard's nerves are understandable. articles.title: Nike y la NFL llevan sus rivalidades históricas a las nuevas camisetas de 2026
articles.standfirst: El programa Rivalries estrena ocho nuevos diseños para los equipos de la NFC North y la AFC South tras convertirse en uno de los grandes éxitos comerciales de la pasada temporada
articles.summary: El programa Rivalries estrena ocho nuevos diseños para los equipos de la NFC North y la AFC South tras convertirse en uno de los grandes éxitos comerciales de la pasada temporada
articles.body: La NFL también juega sus rivalidades fuera del campo. Nike y la liga estadounidense han presentado las nuevas equipaciones de Rivalries para 2026, la segunda temporada de un proyecto que busca trasladar a las camisetas la identidad, historia y orgullo de algunas de las franquicias más reconocibles del campeonato. Este año será el turno de los equipos de la NFC North y la AFC South, con ocho nuevas equipaciones que se estrenarán durante partidos como Green Bay Packers-Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions-Minnesota Vikings o Indianapolis Colts-Houston Texans. Cada uniforme permanecerá durante tres temporadas dentro de la rotación de equipaciones de su franquicia. La apuesta llega después del impacto conseguido en 2025. Según los datos ofrecidos por la organización, el estreno de Rivalries se convirtió en el lanzamiento de merchandising con mayores ventas registrado por Fanatics, un éxito que ha impulsado la expansión del proyecto. Con los ocho conjuntos de la pasada campaña y los ocho que se incorporan ahora, 16 equipos utilizarán diseños Rivalries durante la temporada 2026. Además, Nike y la NFL acompañarán el lanzamiento con campañas protagonizadas por jugadores, leyendas y artistas vinculados a las ciudades de cada franquicia. Las nuevas camisetas y la colección para aficionados saldrán a la venta el próximo 1 de septiembre.

articles.title: NFL reveals 2026 Rivalries uniforms for AFC South, NFC North teams
articles.summary: The uniforms will remain a part of the team's rotation for the next three seasons.
articles.body:
The NFL is bringing back rivalry uniforms for the upcoming 2026 season.

After launching the NFL's Rivalries program in 2025, the league has teamed up with Nike and revealed the uniforms the eight teams in the AFC South and NFC North will wear against division rivals this season. Following the on-field debut, the Rivalries uniforms will be a part of the team's rotation for three years along with its existing looks.

Those teams that wore Rivalries uniforms last season will wear them for a game against a divisional rival in 2026. More teams will join the program during the 2027 and 2028 seasons.

Indianapolis Colts : Week 3 vs. Houston Texans

Green Bay Packers : Week 5 vs. Chicago Bears

Detroit Lions : Week 8 vs. Minnesota Vikings

Jacksonville Jaguars : Week 8 vs. Indianapolis Colts

Tennessee Titans : Week 10 vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

Houston Texans: Week 11 vs. Indianapolis Colts

Minnesota Vikings: Week 15 vs. Detroit Lions

Chicago Bears: Week 16 vs. Green Bay Packers

The eight NFL teams who were part of the initial launch last season will wear them again in 2026, including the Seahawks and Rams , who will face each other in Week 16 wearing their Rivalries uniforms.

Arizona Cardinals : Week 2 vs. Seattle Seahawks Buffalo Bills : Week 11 vs. Miami Dolphins New England : Week 13 vs. Buffalo Bills San Francisco 49ers : Week 14 vs. Los Angeles Rams Seattle Seahawks: Week 16 vs. Los Angeles Rams Los Angeles Rams: Week 16 vs. Seattle Seahawks New York Jets : Week 16 vs. New England Patriots Miami Dolphins: Week 17 vs. Buffalo Bills

In 2027, the AFC West and NFC East will be part of the program, and the AFC North and NFC South will join in 2028.

articles.title: NFL, Disney Drop Collaboration with Apparel for All 32 Teams in New Photos Ahead of 2026 Season
articles.summary: The NFL and Disney collaborated to launch new apparel for all 32 teams ahead of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The NFL and Disney collaborated to launch new apparel for all 32 teams ahead of the 2026 season.

The Disney x Champion NFL Collection includes t-shirts and sweatshirts that feature a character from Disney, Pixar, Marvel or Star Wars matched with each team (h/t AL.com's Josie Howell ).

The collection was previously introduced at Fanatics Fest on July 16, with NFL commissioner Roger Goodell helping to showcase the first eight team-character pairings.

Bret Healey, Disney's director of graphic design at Disney Consumer Products, discussed the design process.

"Today's consumers view fandom as an extension of personal style, and this collection was designed with that mindset from the start," Healey said . "Each piece transforms team affiliation into something expressive, collectible and culturally relevant."

The 2026 season will officially kick off when the Seattle Seahawks face the New England Patriots on Sept. 9 at 8:20 p.m. ET.
